objective.en: Build and cable your first PC-switch-router network, then learn to move between the IOS CLI modes and use context-sensitive help.
objective.hi: Apna pehla PC-switch-router network banao aur cable karo, phir IOS CLI modes ke beech move karna aur context-sensitive help use karna seekho.

tasks.en: Open Packet Tracer. From the device boxes place one 2960 switch (SW1), one 1941 router (R1) and one PC (PC1) on the workspace.
tasks.hi: Packet Tracer kholo. Device boxes se ek 2960 switch (SW1), ek 1941 router (R1) aur ek PC (PC1) workspace par rakho.

tasks.en: Cable it: Connections > Copper Straight-Through from PC1 Fa0 to SW1 F0/1, and another straight-through from SW1 F0/24 to R1 G0/0.
tasks.hi: Cable lagao: Connections > Copper Straight-Through se PC1 Fa0 ko SW1 F0/1 se jodo, aur ek aur straight-through se SW1 F0/24 ko R1 G0/0 se jodo.

tasks.en: Click R1 > CLI tab, press Enter. You are in user EXEC mode (Router> prompt). Type enable to reach privileged EXEC (Router#), then configure terminal to reach global config (Router(config)#).
tasks.hi: R1 > CLI tab par click karo, Enter dabao. Abhi tum user EXEC mode mein ho (Router> prompt). enable type karo toh privileged EXEC (Router#) mein pahunchoge, phir configure terminal se global config (Router(config)#) mein jao.

tasks.en: Rename the router: hostname R1. Watch the prompt change instantly. Type exit to step back one mode, then end (or Ctrl+Z) to jump straight to privileged EXEC.
tasks.hi: Router ka naam badlo: hostname R1. Dekho prompt turant badal jata hai. exit type karo toh ek mode peeche aate ho, phir end (ya Ctrl+Z) se seedha privileged EXEC mein pahunch jao.

tasks.en: Explore help: at the R1# prompt type ? to list commands, then show ? to list show options. Type sh then press Tab to see command completion expand it to show.
tasks.hi: Help explore karo: R1# prompt par ? type karo toh commands ki list aayegi, phir show ? se show ke options dekho. sh type karke Tab dabao aur dekho command completion use show mein expand kar deta hai.

tasks.en: Run show version and find the IOS version and the number of interfaces. Run show running-config and find your hostname near the top.
tasks.hi: show version chalao aur IOS version aur interfaces ki ginti dhoondo. show running-config chalao aur upar ki taraf apna hostname dhoondo.

tasks.en: On R1, bring the LAN interface up: configure terminal, interface g0/0, no shutdown, end.
tasks.hi: R1 par LAN interface up karo: configure terminal, interface g0/0, no shutdown, end.

tasks.en: Click SW1 > CLI, press Enter, then: enable, configure terminal, hostname SW1, end. Save on both devices with copy running-config startup-config.
tasks.hi: SW1 > CLI par click karo, Enter dabao, phir: enable, configure terminal, hostname SW1, end. Dono devices par copy running-config startup-config se save karo.

verify.en: show version — IOS version, uptime and interface summary are displayed on R1
verify.hi: show version — R1 par IOS version, uptime aur interface summary dikhte hain

verify.en: show running-config — the line 'hostname R1' appears near the top
verify.hi: show running-config — 'hostname R1' wali line upar ki taraf dikhti hai

verify.en: Workspace link lights — both links show green triangles (switch ports take about 30 seconds to turn green while spanning tree checks the port)
verify.hi: Workspace link lights — dono links par green triangles dikhte hain (switch ports ko green hone mein lagbhag 30 seconds lagte hain jab tak spanning tree port check karta hai)

verify.en: show startup-config — matches running-config after the save
verify.hi: show startup-config — save ke baad running-config se match karta hai

note.en: Prompt cheat-sheet: Router> = user EXEC, Router# = privileged EXEC, Router(config)# = global config, Router(config-if)# = interface config. You will live in these four modes for the whole course.
note.hi: Prompt cheat-sheet: Router> = user EXEC, Router# = privileged EXEC, Router(config)# = global config, Router(config-if)# = interface config. Poore course mein tum inhi chaar modes mein rahoge.

objective.en: Assemble a small two-tier (collapsed core) topology and pick the correct copper cable type for every link.
objective.hi: Ek chhota two-tier (collapsed core) topology banao aur har link ke liye sahi copper cable type chuno.

topology: R1 (G0/0) — (G0/1) SW-DIST; SW-DIST (F0/1) — (F0/1) SW-ACC; SW-ACC (F0/2) — PC1; SW-ACC (F0/3) — PC2

tasks.en: Place one 1941 router (R1), two 2960 switches (rename them SW-DIST and SW-ACC via hostname), and two PCs.
tasks.hi: Ek 1941 router (R1), do 2960 switches (hostname se inka naam SW-DIST aur SW-ACC rakho), aur do PCs rakho.

tasks.en: Connect PC1 and PC2 to SW-ACC F0/2 and F0/3 with Copper Straight-Through cables (unlike devices: PC to switch).
tasks.hi: PC1 aur PC2 ko SW-ACC F0/2 aur F0/3 se Copper Straight-Through cables se jodo (unlike devices: PC se switch).

tasks.en: Deliberately connect SW-ACC F0/1 to SW-DIST F0/1 with a Copper Straight-Through cable and observe the link lights stay red — like devices need a crossover.
tasks.hi: Jaan-boojh kar SW-ACC F0/1 ko SW-DIST F0/1 se Copper Straight-Through cable se jodo aur dekho link lights red hi rehti hain — like devices ko crossover chahiye.

tasks.en: Delete that cable and replace it with Copper Cross-Over. Watch the lights go amber then green.
tasks.hi: Woh cable delete karo aur uski jagah Copper Cross-Over lagao. Dekho lights pehle amber phir green hoti hain.

tasks.en: Connect SW-DIST G0/1 to R1 G0/0 with straight-through, then on R1: interface g0/0 and no shutdown.
tasks.hi: SW-DIST G0/1 ko R1 G0/0 se straight-through se jodo, phir R1 par: interface g0/0 aur no shutdown.

tasks.en: On paper, label each device with its tier: R1 plus SW-DIST form the collapsed core/distribution layer, SW-ACC is the access layer. Sketch how a 3-tier design would differ (separate core switches).
tasks.hi: Paper par har device par uska tier likho: R1 aur SW-DIST milkar collapsed core/distribution layer banate hain, SW-ACC access layer hai. Sketch karo ki 3-tier design kaise alag hota (alag core switches).

tasks.en: On paper, list which cable you would use for: PC-to-switch, switch-to-switch, router-to-switch, and PC directly to router (straight, cross, straight, cross).
tasks.hi: Paper par likho ki in links ke liye kaunsa cable use karoge: PC-to-switch, switch-to-switch, router-to-switch, aur PC seedha router se (straight, cross, straight, cross).

tasks.en: Hover the mouse over each device in Packet Tracer and note the port status list that pops up.
tasks.hi: Packet Tracer mein har device par mouse hover karo aur jo port status list pop up hoti hai use note karo.

verify.en: Workspace link lights — every link green after replacing the wrong cable
verify.hi: Workspace link lights — galat cable badalne ke baad har link green

verify.en: show interfaces status (on SW-ACC) — F0/1, F0/2, F0/3 show 'connected'
verify.hi: show interfaces status (SW-ACC par) — F0/1, F0/2, F0/3 'connected' dikhate hain

verify.en: Your paper sketch — 2-tier collapses core and distribution into one layer; 3-tier separates them
verify.hi: Tumhara paper sketch — 2-tier mein core aur distribution ek hi layer mein collapse ho jaate hain; 3-tier mein dono alag hote hain

note.en: Modern switches do auto-MDIX so crossover rarely matters in real life, but the exam still tests classic cable-selection rules, and Packet Tracer enforces them on some models.
note.hi: Modern switches auto-MDIX karte hain isliye real life mein crossover kam hi matter karta hai, lekin exam abhi bhi classic cable-selection rules test karta hai, aur Packet Tracer kuch models par inhe enforce karta hai.

objective.en: Watch a switch learn MAC addresses, then control interface speed and duplex and read the interface counters.
objective.hi: Dekho switch MAC addresses kaise seekhta hai, phir interface speed aur duplex control karo aur interface counters padho.

tasks.en: Build the topology: one 2960 (SW1) and two PCs on F0/1 and F0/2 with straight-through cables.
tasks.hi: Topology banao: ek 2960 (SW1) aur do PCs F0/1 aur F0/2 par, straight-through cables se.

tasks.en: Give the PCs addresses in the same subnet: PC1 Desktop > IP Configuration > 192.168.1.11 mask 255.255.255.0; PC2 192.168.1.12 mask 255.255.255.0.
tasks.hi: PCs ko same subnet mein addresses do: PC1 Desktop > IP Configuration > 192.168.1.11 mask 255.255.255.0; PC2 192.168.1.12 mask 255.255.255.0.

tasks.en: On each PC open Desktop > Command Prompt and run ipconfig /all. Write down each PC's MAC (physical) address.
tasks.hi: Har PC par Desktop > Command Prompt kholo aur ipconfig /all chalao. Har PC ka MAC (physical) address likh lo.

tasks.en: On SW1 run show mac address-table — the dynamic table should be empty (or nearly) before any traffic.
tasks.hi: SW1 par show mac address-table chalao — kisi bhi traffic se pehle dynamic table khaali (ya lagbhag khaali) honi chahiye.

tasks.en: From PC1 ping 192.168.1.12. Then on SW1 run show mac address-table dynamic and match the two learned MACs to ports F0/1 and F0/2 and to the addresses you wrote down.
tasks.hi: PC1 se ping 192.168.1.12 karo. Phir SW1 par show mac address-table dynamic chalao aur dono learned MACs ko ports F0/1 aur F0/2 se aur apne likhe hue addresses se match karo.

tasks.en: Hard-set the PC1 port: on SW1, interface f0/1 then speed 100 and duplex full.
tasks.hi: PC1 wala port hard-set karo: SW1 par interface f0/1 phir speed 100 aur duplex full.

tasks.en: Run show interfaces f0/1 and find the line reporting 'Full-duplex, 100Mb/s'. Also locate the counters for runts, giants, CRC and collisions (all should be 0).
tasks.hi: show interfaces f0/1 chalao aur woh line dhoondo jo 'Full-duplex, 100Mb/s' report karti hai. Runts, giants, CRC aur collisions ke counters bhi dhoondo (sab 0 hone chahiye).

tasks.en: Set the same speed/duplex on PC1: PC1 > Config > FastEthernet0 > uncheck auto-negotiate equivalents by selecting 100 Mbps and Full Duplex, then re-run the ping to confirm nothing broke.
tasks.hi: PC1 par bhi same speed/duplex set karo: PC1 > Config > FastEthernet0 > 100 Mbps aur Full Duplex select karke auto-negotiate jaisi settings hatao, phir ping dobara chalao aur confirm karo ki kuch toota nahi.

verify.en: show mac address-table dynamic — exactly one MAC on F0/1 and one on F0/2, matching the PCs' ipconfig /all output
verify.hi: show mac address-table dynamic — F0/1 par theek ek MAC aur F0/2 par ek, jo PCs ke ipconfig /all output se match karte hain

verify.en: show interfaces f0/1 — reports Full-duplex, 100Mb/s and the interface is up/up
verify.hi: show interfaces f0/1 — Full-duplex, 100Mb/s report karta hai aur interface up/up hai

verify.en: ping 192.168.1.12 from PC1 — 4 replies (first ping may lose one packet to ARP)
verify.hi: PC1 se ping 192.168.1.12 — 4 replies (pehle ping mein ARP ki wajah se ek packet lose ho sakta hai)

note.en: A duplex mismatch (one side full, one side half) still links up but causes late collisions and terrible performance — a classic exam and real-world troubleshooting scenario.
note.hi: Duplex mismatch (ek side full, ek side half) mein link phir bhi up ho jata hai lekin late collisions aur bahut kharab performance aati hai — yeh exam aur real-world troubleshooting dono ka classic scenario hai.

objective.en: Configure IPv4 addresses on PCs and a router interface, set default gateways, and prove connectivity with ping.
objective.hi: PCs aur ek router interface par IPv4 addresses configure karo, default gateways set karo, aur ping se connectivity prove karo.

tasks.en: Build the topology with a 2960 (SW1), a 1941 (R1) and two PCs.
tasks.hi: Ek 2960 (SW1), ek 1941 (R1) aur do PCs ke saath topology banao.

tasks.en: On R1: configure terminal, interface g0/0, ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown, end.
tasks.hi: R1 par: configure terminal, interface g0/0, ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown, end.

tasks.en: On PC1: Desktop > IP Configuration > static 192.168.10.11, mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.10.1.
tasks.hi: PC1 par: Desktop > IP Configuration > static 192.168.10.11, mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.10.1.

tasks.en: From PC1 ping 192.168.10.12 (PC2), then ping 192.168.10.1 (the router).
tasks.hi: PC1 se ping 192.168.10.12 (PC2) karo, phir ping 192.168.10.1 (router) karo.

tasks.en: On R1 run show ip interface brief and confirm G0/0 shows your address with Status up and Protocol up.
tasks.hi: R1 par show ip interface brief chalao aur confirm karo ki G0/0 tumhara address Status up aur Protocol up ke saath dikha raha hai.

tasks.en: Break it on purpose: change PC2's mask to 255.255.255.128 (/25). PC2 at .12 now believes it is in 192.168.10.0/25 — ping still works from PC1 because both are below .128. Now change PC2's address to 192.168.10.140 keeping /25 and watch pings to the .1 gateway fail (gateway is outside PC2's new subnet).
tasks.hi: Jaan-boojh kar todo: PC2 ka mask 255.255.255.128 (/25) kar do. Ab .12 wala PC2 samajhta hai ki woh 192.168.10.0/25 mein hai — PC1 se ping phir bhi chalta hai kyunki dono .128 se neeche hain. Ab PC2 ka address 192.168.10.140 kar do, /25 rakhte hue, aur dekho .1 gateway ko pings fail hote hain (gateway PC2 ke naye subnet ke bahar hai).

tasks.en: Restore PC2 to 192.168.10.12 mask 255.255.255.0 and re-verify the pings.
tasks.hi: PC2 ko wapas 192.168.10.12 mask 255.255.255.0 par restore karo aur pings dobara verify karo.

tasks.en: On paper classify these addresses as private or public: 10.0.0.5, 172.20.1.1, 172.32.1.1, 192.168.5.9, 8.8.8.8 (private, private, public, private, public).
tasks.hi: Paper par in addresses ko private ya public mein classify karo: 10.0.0.5, 172.20.1.1, 172.32.1.1, 192.168.5.9, 8.8.8.8 (private, private, public, private, public).

verify.en: show ip interface brief — GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up
verify.hi: show ip interface brief — GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 up/up

verify.en: ping 192.168.10.12 from PC1 — success
verify.hi: PC1 se ping 192.168.10.12 — success

verify.en: ping 192.168.10.1 from PC2 after restoring settings — success
verify.hi: settings restore karne ke baad PC2 se ping 192.168.10.1 — success

title.hi: Ek /24 ko Chaar Networks mein Subnet karo

objective.en: Split 192.168.1.0/24 into four equal /26 subnets, document them, and address a two-LAN router topology from your plan.
objective.hi: 192.168.1.0/24 ko chaar barabar /26 subnets mein todo, unhe document karo, aur apne plan se ek two-LAN router topology ko address karo.

tasks.en: On paper, divide 192.168.1.0/24 into four /26 subnets. Block size is 64, so the networks are 192.168.1.0, 192.168.1.64, 192.168.1.128 and 192.168.1.192.
tasks.hi: Paper par 192.168.1.0/24 ko chaar /26 subnets mein divide karo. Block size 64 hai, isliye networks hain 192.168.1.0, 192.168.1.64, 192.168.1.128 aur 192.168.1.192.

tasks.en: For each subnet write a table row: network address, first usable, last usable, broadcast. (Example: 192.168.1.64/26 — first .65, last .126, broadcast .127.)
tasks.hi: Har subnet ke liye ek table row likho: network address, first usable, last usable, broadcast. (Example: 192.168.1.64/26 — first .65, last .126, broadcast .127.)

tasks.en: Build the topology: R1 (1941), two 2960 switches, four PCs (two per switch).
tasks.hi: Topology banao: R1 (1941), do 2960 switches, chaar PCs (har switch par do).

tasks.en: Assign subnet 1 to LAN A: R1 interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.192, no shutdown. PC1 = 192.168.1.11, PC2 = 192.168.1.12, mask 255.255.255.192, gateway 192.168.1.1.
Assign subnet 2 to LAN B: R1 interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.1.65 255.255.255.192, no shutdown. PC3 = 192.168.1.75, PC4 = 192.168.1.76, mask 255.255.255.192, gateway 192.168.1.65.
From PC1 ping PC2 (same subnet, switched) then ping PC3 (different subnet — the router forwards it).
tasks.hi: PC1 se PC2 ko ping karo (same subnet, switched) phir PC3 ko ping karo (alag subnet — router ise forward karta hai).

tasks.en: On R1 run show ip route and identify the two connected (C) routes and two local (L) routes.
tasks.hi: R1 par show ip route chalao aur do connected (C) routes aur do local (L) routes pehchano.

tasks.en: Sanity-check your table: try to assign 192.168.1.63 to a PC and explain why it must never be used (it is subnet 1's broadcast address).
tasks.hi: Apni table ka sanity-check karo: 192.168.1.63 kisi PC ko dene ki koshish karo aur samjhao ki yeh kabhi use kyun nahi hona chahiye (yeh subnet 1 ka broadcast address hai).

verify.en: show ip route — C 192.168.1.0/26 and C 192.168.1.64/26 both present
verify.hi: show ip route — C 192.168.1.0/26 aur C 192.168.1.64/26 dono present

verify.en: ping from PC1 to 192.168.1.75 — success across the router
verify.hi: PC1 se 192.168.1.75 ko ping — router ke paar success

verify.en: Your subnet table — 4 rows, broadcast addresses .63, .127, .191, .255
verify.hi: Tumhari subnet table — 4 rows, broadcast addresses .63, .127, .191, .255

note.en: /26 = mask 255.255.255.192 = block size 64 = 62 usable hosts per subnet. Say it until it is automatic.
note.hi: /26 = mask 255.255.255.192 = block size 64 = har subnet mein 62 usable hosts. Itni baar bolo ki automatic ho jaye.

title.hi: Magic-Number Speed Drill (Live Proof ke saath)

objective.en: Drill the magic-number method on paper under time pressure, then prove two of your answers in Packet Tracer by predicting whether pings will succeed.
objective.hi: Time pressure mein paper par magic-number method ki practice karo, phir Packet Tracer mein pings succeed honge ya nahi yeh predict karke apne do answers prove karo.

tasks.en: From memory, write the two magic-number reference rows: mask octet values 128 192 224 240 248 252 254 255 and their block sizes 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1. Check yourself, then rewrite until perfect.
tasks.hi: Yaad se do magic-number reference rows likho: mask octet values 128 192 224 240 248 252 254 255 aur unke block sizes 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1. Khud check karo, phir tab tak dobara likho jab tak perfect na ho.

tasks.en: Timed drill (aim under 60 seconds each) — for 10.44.129.77/19 find network, broadcast and usable range. (Answer: 10.44.128.0, 10.44.159.255, 10.44.128.1 to 10.44.159.254.)
tasks.hi: Timed drill (har ek 60 seconds se kam mein karne ka target) — 10.44.129.77/19 ke liye network, broadcast aur usable range nikalo. (Answer: 10.44.128.0, 10.44.159.255, 10.44.128.1 se 10.44.159.254.)

tasks.en: Prediction test: build PC1 — SW1 — PC2. Set PC1 = 172.16.91.190 mask 255.255.255.192 and PC2 = 172.16.91.200 mask 255.255.255.192. Using your answers, predict whether PC1 can ping PC2 before you try.
tasks.hi: Prediction test: PC1 — SW1 — PC2 banao. PC1 = 172.16.91.190 mask 255.255.255.192 aur PC2 = 172.16.91.200 mask 255.255.255.192 set karo. Apne answers use karke try karne se pehle predict karo ki PC1, PC2 ko ping kar payega ya nahi.

tasks.en: Run the ping. It fails: .190 lives in the 172.16.91.128/26 subnet while .200 lives in 172.16.91.192/26, and with no gateway configured the packet has nowhere to go.
tasks.hi: Ping chalao. Yeh fail hota hai: .190 172.16.91.128/26 subnet mein hai jabki .200 172.16.91.192/26 mein hai, aur koi gateway configured nahi hai toh packet ke paas jaane ki koi jagah nahi.

tasks.en: Now move PC1 to 172.16.91.201 mask 255.255.255.192, predict again, and confirm the ping succeeds (same subnet).
tasks.hi: Ab PC1 ko 172.16.91.201 mask 255.255.255.192 par le jao, phir se predict karo, aur confirm karo ki ping succeed hota hai (same subnet).

tasks.en: Repeat the drill cycle with three self-invented problems; stop only when all three are correct in under 60 seconds each.
tasks.hi: Teen khud banaye problems ke saath drill cycle repeat karo; tabhi ruko jab teeno har ek 60 seconds se kam mein sahi ho jayein.

verify.en: ping test 1 (PC1 .190 to PC2 .200) — Request timed out, matching your prediction
verify.hi: ping test 1 (PC1 .190 se PC2 .200) — Request timed out, tumhare prediction se match

verify.en: ping test 2 (PC1 .201 to PC2 .200) — success, matching your prediction
verify.hi: ping test 2 (PC1 .201 se PC2 .200) — success, tumhare prediction se match

verify.en: Drill sheet — 6 of 6 problems correct with network and broadcast identified
verify.hi: Drill sheet — 6 mein se 6 problems sahi, network aur broadcast identify kiye hue

note.en: Magic number = 256 minus the interesting mask octet. Count up in that block size to bracket the address; network is the lower bound, broadcast is one below the next block.
note.hi: Magic number = 256 minus interesting mask octet. Us block size mein upar ginte jao jab tak address bracket na ho jaye; network lower bound hai, broadcast agle block se ek kam.

objective.en: Design a VLSM plan for four differently-sized networks from a single /24, then implement two of the LANs plus the WAN link in Packet Tracer.
objective.hi: Ek hi /24 se chaar alag-alag size ke networks ke liye VLSM plan design karo, phir Packet Tracer mein do LANs aur WAN link implement karo.

tasks.en: Requirements from 192.168.100.0/24: Sales LAN 60 hosts, Support LAN 28 hosts, Guest LAN 12 hosts, and two router-to-router WAN links (2 hosts each). Allocate largest first.
tasks.hi: 192.168.100.0/24 se requirements: Sales LAN 60 hosts, Support LAN 28 hosts, Guest LAN 12 hosts, aur do router-to-router WAN links (har ek mein 2 hosts). Sabse bada pehle allocate karo.

tasks.en: For each allocation write network, mask in dotted decimal, first/last usable and broadcast in a table.
tasks.hi: Har allocation ke liye ek table mein network, dotted decimal mein mask, first/last usable aur broadcast likho.

tasks.en: Build the topology with two 1941 routers, two switches and two PCs.
tasks.hi: Do 1941 routers, do switches aur do PCs ke saath topology banao.

tasks.en: Configure Sales: R1 interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.100.1 255.255.255.192, no shutdown; PC1 = 192.168.100.10 mask 255.255.255.192 gateway 192.168.100.1.
tasks.hi: Sales configure karo: R1 interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.100.1 255.255.255.192, no shutdown; PC1 = 192.168.100.10 mask 255.255.255.192 gateway 192.168.100.1.

tasks.en: Configure the WAN-A link: R1 interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.100.113 255.255.255.252, no shutdown; R2 interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.100.114 255.255.255.252, no shutdown.
tasks.hi: WAN-A link configure karo: R1 interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.100.113 255.255.255.252, no shutdown; R2 interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.100.114 255.255.255.252, no shutdown.

tasks.en: Configure Support: R2 interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.100.65 255.255.255.224, no shutdown; PC2 = 192.168.100.70 mask 255.255.255.224 gateway 192.168.100.65.
tasks.hi: Support configure karo: R2 interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.100.65 255.255.255.224, no shutdown; PC2 = 192.168.100.70 mask 255.255.255.224 gateway 192.168.100.65.

tasks.en: Test what connected routes alone can do: from R1 ping 192.168.100.114 (works — connected WAN). From PC1 ping PC2 (fails — R2 has no route back to the Sales subnet; routing arrives in week 5).
tasks.hi: Test karo ki sirf connected routes kya kar sakte hain: R1 se ping 192.168.100.114 (chalta hai — connected WAN). PC1 se PC2 ko ping (fail — R2 ke paas Sales subnet ka return route nahi hai; routing week 5 mein aayegi).

verify.en: Your VLSM table — allocations do not overlap and each mask matches the host count
verify.hi: Tumhari VLSM table — allocations overlap nahi karte aur har mask host count se match karta hai

verify.en: ping 192.168.100.114 from R1 — success across the WAN /30
verify.hi: R1 se ping 192.168.100.114 — WAN /30 ke paar success

verify.en: show ip route on R1 — connected routes for 192.168.100.0/26 and 192.168.100.112/30 only
verify.hi: R1 par show ip route — sirf 192.168.100.0/26 aur 192.168.100.112/30 ke connected routes

verify.en: ping from PC1 to PC2 — fails, and you can explain why (no return route yet)
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ko ping — fail, aur tum samjha sakte ho kyun (abhi return route nahi hai)

note.en: VLSM rule: sort requirements from largest to smallest and allocate in that order — it prevents overlap and wasted space.
note.hi: VLSM rule: requirements ko sabse bade se sabse chhote tak sort karo aur usi order mein allocate karo — isse overlap aur wasted space nahi hota.

objective.en: Enable IPv6 routing, assign global unicast and link-local addresses to a router, and address a PC statically.
objective.hi: IPv6 routing enable karo, router ko global unicast aur link-local addresses do, aur ek PC ko statically address karo.

tasks.en: Build the topology (2960, 1941, one PC).
tasks.hi: Topology banao (2960, 1941, ek PC).

tasks.en: On R1 enable IPv6 forwarding: configure terminal, then ipv6 unicast-routing.
tasks.hi: R1 par IPv6 forwarding enable karo: configure terminal, phir ipv6 unicast-routing.

tasks.en: Address the interface: interface g0/0, ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:1::1/64, and give it a memorable link-local with ipv6 address fe80::1 link-local, then no shutdown.
tasks.hi: Interface ko address do: interface g0/0, ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:1::1/64, aur ipv6 address fe80::1 link-local se ek yaad rehne wala link-local do, phir no shutdown.

tasks.en: Run show ipv6 interface g0/0 and identify: the link-local (fe80::1), the global unicast, and the joined multicast groups (ff02::1 all-nodes, ff02::2 all-routers, plus a solicited-node ff02::1:ff... address).
tasks.hi: show ipv6 interface g0/0 chalao aur pehchano: link-local (fe80::1), global unicast, aur joined multicast groups (ff02::1 all-nodes, ff02::2 all-routers, plus ek solicited-node ff02::1:ff... address).

tasks.en: On PC1: Desktop > IP Configuration > IPv6 static: 2001:db8:acad:1::10 prefix /64, gateway fe80::1.
tasks.hi: PC1 par: Desktop > IP Configuration > IPv6 static: 2001:db8:acad:1::10 prefix /64, gateway fe80::1.

tasks.en: From PC1 ping 2001:db8:acad:1::1.
tasks.hi: PC1 se ping 2001:db8:acad:1::1 karo.

Paper par in addresses ko poori tarah compress karo: 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329 aur fe80:0000:0000:0000:0204:61ff:fe9d:f156. (Answers: 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329 aur fe80::204:61ff:fe9d:f156.)

tasks.en: On paper, name the address types: fe80::/10 link-local, ff02:: multicast, 2000::/3 global unicast, ::1 loopback, fc00::/7 unique local.
tasks.hi: Paper par address types ke naam likho: fe80::/10 link-local, ff02:: multicast, 2000::/3 global unicast, ::1 loopback, fc00::/7 unique local.

verify.en: show ipv6 interface brief — G0/0 lists fe80::1 and 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1
verify.hi: show ipv6 interface brief — G0/0 par fe80::1 aur 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1 listed hain

verify.en: ping 2001:db8:acad:1::1 from PC1 — success
verify.hi: PC1 se ping 2001:db8:acad:1::1 — success

verify.en: Your compression answers — match the answers given in the task
verify.hi: Tumhare compression answers — task mein diye answers se match karte hain

note.en: Compression rules: drop leading zeros in each group; replace exactly ONE longest run of all-zero groups with ::. Two :: in one address is illegal because it becomes ambiguous.
note.hi: Compression rules: har group ke leading zeros hata do; all-zero groups ki sirf EK sabse lambi run ko :: se replace karo. Ek address mein do :: illegal hain kyunki address ambiguous ho jata hai.

objective.en: Configure a router to hand out prefixes for SLAAC, generate an EUI-64 interface ID, and verify how clients autoconfigure.
objective.hi: Router ko SLAAC ke liye prefixes dene ke liye configure karo, EUI-64 interface ID generate karo, aur verify karo ki clients kaise autoconfigure hote hain.

tasks.en: Build the topology and on R1 enable ipv6 unicast-routing (this also makes the router send Router Advertisements).
tasks.hi: Topology banao aur R1 par ipv6 unicast-routing enable karo (isse router Router Advertisements bhi bhejne lagta hai).

tasks.en: Address LAN 1: interface g0/0, ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:1::1/64, no shutdown.
tasks.hi: LAN 1 ko address do: interface g0/0, ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:1::1/64, no shutdown.

tasks.en: Address LAN 2 using EUI-64: interface g0/1, ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:2::/64 eui-64, no shutdown.
tasks.hi: LAN 2 ko EUI-64 se address do: interface g0/1, ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:2::/64 eui-64, no shutdown.

tasks.en: Run show ipv6 interface g0/1 and inspect the global address: the interface ID was built from the interface MAC with FFFE inserted in the middle and the 7th bit flipped. Write down the MAC and confirm the transformation by hand.
tasks.hi: show ipv6 interface g0/1 chalao aur global address dekho: interface ID interface ke MAC se bana hai, beech mein FFFE insert hua hai aur 7th bit flip hua hai. MAC likh lo aur haath se transformation confirm karo.

tasks.en: On PC1 choose Desktop > IP Configuration > IPv6 > Automatic. The PC listens for R1's Router Advertisement and builds its own address from the 2001:db8:acad:1::/64 prefix.
tasks.hi: PC1 par Desktop > IP Configuration > IPv6 > Automatic chuno. PC R1 ka Router Advertisement sunta hai aur 2001:db8:acad:1::/64 prefix se apna address khud banata hai.

tasks.en: On PC2 do the same (it should autoconfigure from 2001:db8:acad:2::/64).
tasks.hi: PC2 par bhi yahi karo (yeh 2001:db8:acad:2::/64 se autoconfigure hona chahiye).

tasks.en: From PC1 ping PC2's autoconfigured global address (read it from PC2's IP Configuration window).
tasks.hi: PC1 se PC2 ke autoconfigured global address ko ping karo (address PC2 ki IP Configuration window se padho).

tasks.en: Run show ipv6 neighbors on R1 — this is the IPv6 equivalent of the ARP table, populated by Neighbor Discovery (NDP), which replaced ARP entirely in IPv6.
tasks.hi: R1 par show ipv6 neighbors chalao — yeh ARP table ka IPv6 version hai, jo Neighbor Discovery (NDP) se bharta hai; IPv6 mein NDP ne ARP ko poori tarah replace kar diya hai.

verify.en: show ipv6 interface g0/1 — global address contains FF:FE in the middle of the interface ID
verify.hi: show ipv6 interface g0/1 — global address mein interface ID ke beech FF:FE hai

verify.en: PC1 IP Configuration — automatic address starting 2001:DB8:ACAD:1:
verify.hi: PC1 IP Configuration — 2001:DB8:ACAD:1: se shuru hone wala automatic address

verify.en: ping PC2's global address from PC1 — success
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ke global address ko ping — success

verify.en: show ipv6 neighbors on R1 — entries for both PCs after the ping
verify.hi: R1 par show ipv6 neighbors — ping ke baad dono PCs ki entries

note.en: EUI-64 by hand: split the 48-bit MAC in half, insert FFFE, then flip bit 7 of the first byte (e.g. 00 becomes 02). The exam loves asking for the flipped bit.
note.hi: EUI-64 haath se: 48-bit MAC ko aadha-aadha todo, beech mein FFFE daalo, phir first byte ka bit 7 flip karo (jaise 00 ban jata hai 02). Exam ko flipped bit poochna bahut pasand hai.

title.en: Watch TCP and UDP on the Wire
title.hi: Wire par TCP aur UDP dekho

objective.en: Use Packet Tracer Simulation mode to watch the TCP three-way handshake for HTTP and contrast it with connectionless UDP for DNS.
objective.hi: Packet Tracer Simulation mode use karke HTTP ke liye TCP three-way handshake dekho aur DNS ke connectionless UDP se uska contrast karo.

topology: PC1 (Fa0) — (F0/1) SW1 (F0/24) — (Fa0) Server1 (HTTP and DNS services)

tasks.en: Build the topology with a generic Server-PT. Address PC1 = 192.168.20.11/24 and Server1 = 192.168.20.10/24 (no gateway needed).
tasks.hi: Ek generic Server-PT ke saath topology banao. PC1 = 192.168.20.11/24 aur Server1 = 192.168.20.10/24 address do (gateway ki zaroorat nahi).

tasks.en: On Server1 > Services confirm HTTP is On. Under DNS, turn the service On and add an A record: name www.ccna.lab, address 192.168.20.10.
tasks.hi: Server1 > Services par confirm karo ki HTTP On hai. DNS ke andar service On karo aur ek A record add karo: name www.ccna.lab, address 192.168.20.10.

tasks.en: On PC1 > Desktop > IP Configuration set DNS server = 192.168.20.10.
tasks.hi: PC1 > Desktop > IP Configuration par DNS server = 192.168.20.10 set karo.

tasks.en: Realtime test: PC1 > Desktop > Web Browser, open http://www.ccna.lab — the demo page should load.
tasks.hi: Realtime test: PC1 > Desktop > Web Browser, http://www.ccna.lab kholo — demo page load hona chahiye.

tasks.en: Switch to Simulation mode (bottom-right toggle). Edit Filters and leave only DNS, TCP and HTTP checked.
tasks.hi: Simulation mode par switch karo (bottom-right toggle). Edit Filters mein sirf DNS, TCP aur HTTP checked rehne do.

tasks.en: In the browser press Go again and step through with Capture/Forward. First observe the DNS query leave PC1 — click the packet and confirm in the OSI/PDU details that it is UDP with destination port 53, and that no handshake happens before it.
tasks.hi: Browser mein dobara Go dabao aur Capture/Forward se step-by-step chalo. Pehle dekho DNS query PC1 se nikalti hai — packet par click karo aur OSI/PDU details mein confirm karo ki yeh UDP hai destination port 53 ke saath, aur isse pehle koi handshake nahi hota.

tasks.en: Continue stepping: watch the TCP three-way handshake to the server — a segment with SYN, the reply with SYN+ACK, then the final ACK — before any HTTP data moves. Click each packet and read the flags in the PDU details.
tasks.hi: Stepping jaari rakho: server ke saath TCP three-way handshake dekho — SYN wala segment, SYN+ACK wala reply, phir final ACK — yeh sab kisi bhi HTTP data ke move hone se pehle hota hai. Har packet par click karo aur PDU details mein flags padho.

tasks.en: Find the HTTP GET packet and confirm its TCP destination port is 80. Then watch the connection teardown (FIN/ACK exchanges) at the end.
tasks.hi: HTTP GET packet dhoondo aur confirm karo ki uska TCP destination port 80 hai. Phir end mein connection teardown (FIN/ACK exchanges) dekho.

tasks.en: On paper list the well-known ports: FTP 20/21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, TFTP 69, HTTP 80, POP3 110, NTP 123, SNMP 161/162, HTTPS 443, RDP 3389.
tasks.hi: Paper par well-known ports list karo: FTP 20/21, SSH 22, Telnet 23, SMTP 25, DNS 53, DHCP 67/68, TFTP 69, HTTP 80, POP3 110, NTP 123, SNMP 161/162, HTTPS 443, RDP 3389.

verify.en: Simulation PDU details — DNS query uses UDP destination port 53 with no prior handshake
verify.hi: Simulation PDU details — DNS query UDP destination port 53 use karti hai, pehle koi handshake nahi

verify.en: Simulation event list — SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK appear in that order before the HTTP GET
verify.hi: Simulation event list — HTTP GET se pehle SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK isi order mein aate hain

verify.en: HTTP GET PDU — TCP destination port 80
verify.hi: HTTP GET PDU — TCP destination port 80

verify.en: Web page — loads in Realtime mode by name, proving DNS plus TCP both work
verify.hi: Web page — Realtime mode mein naam se load hota hai, jo prove karta hai ki DNS aur TCP dono kaam kar rahe hain

note.en: TCP = reliable, ordered, connection-oriented (handshake, sequence numbers, ACKs). UDP = fire-and-forget, lower overhead — ideal for DNS queries, voice and video.
note.hi: TCP = reliable, ordered, connection-oriented (handshake, sequence numbers, ACKs). UDP = fire-and-forget, kam overhead — DNS queries, voice aur video ke liye ideal.

objective.en: Produce a one-page virtualization design comparing hypervisor types and VMs versus containers, then demonstrate service consolidation on a single Packet Tracer server.
objective.hi: Ek page ka virtualization design banao jisme hypervisor types aur VMs vs containers compare hon, phir ek hi Packet Tracer server par service consolidation demonstrate karo.

topology: PC1 (Fa0) — (F0/1) SW1 (F0/24) — (Fa0) Server1 (HTTP, DNS and DHCP all on one box)

tasks.en: On paper, sketch a type-1 (bare-metal) hypervisor: hardware at the bottom, hypervisor directly on it, three VMs on top (Web, App, DB), each with its own guest OS. Label ESXi/Hyper-V/KVM as examples.
tasks.hi: Paper par type-1 (bare-metal) hypervisor sketch karo: sabse neeche hardware, uske upar seedha hypervisor, sabse upar teen VMs (Web, App, DB), har ek ka apna guest OS. Examples ke roop mein ESXi/Hyper-V/KVM label karo.

tasks.en: Next to it sketch a type-2 (hosted) hypervisor: hardware, host OS, hypervisor app (VirtualBox/VMware Workstation), then the VMs. Note type-2 is for desktops/labs, type-1 for data centers.
tasks.hi: Uske bagal mein type-2 (hosted) hypervisor sketch karo: hardware, host OS, hypervisor app (VirtualBox/VMware Workstation), phir VMs. Note karo ki type-2 desktops/labs ke liye hai, type-1 data centers ke liye.

tasks.en: Write a 5-row comparison table VM vs container: guest OS (full OS vs shares host kernel), size (GBs vs MBs), boot time (minutes vs seconds), isolation (strong vs process-level), examples (ESXi VM vs Docker).
tasks.hi: VM vs container ki 5-row comparison table likho: guest OS (full OS vs host kernel share karta hai), size (GBs vs MBs), boot time (minutes vs seconds), isolation (strong vs process-level), examples (ESXi VM vs Docker).

tasks.en: Write 2-3 sentences defining a VRF: multiple independent routing tables on one physical router, so overlapping customer addresses can coexist — virtualization applied to routing.
tasks.hi: 2-3 sentences mein VRF define karo: ek physical router par multiple independent routing tables, taaki overlapping customer addresses saath mein reh sakein — yaani routing par lagaya gaya virtualization.

tasks.en: Design the virtual networking for your sketch: each VM gets a vNIC connected to a vSwitch, which maps to the host's physical NIC. Add addresses 10.10.10.11-13/24 for the three VMs, gateway 10.10.10.1.
tasks.hi: Apne sketch ke liye virtual networking design karo: har VM ko ek vNIC milta hai jo vSwitch se connected hota hai, aur vSwitch host ke physical NIC se map hota hai. Teen VMs ke liye addresses 10.10.10.11-13/24 aur gateway 10.10.10.1 add karo.

tasks.en: Now the consolidation demo in Packet Tracer (one physical box, three services — the same economics that drive virtualization): build the topology, give Server1 static IP 192.168.30.10/24.
tasks.hi: Ab Packet Tracer mein consolidation demo (ek physical box, teen services — wahi economics jo virtualization ko drive karti hai): topology banao, Server1 ko static IP 192.168.30.10/24 do.

tasks.en: On Server1 > Services enable DHCP: default gateway 192.168.30.10, DNS server 192.168.30.10, start IP 192.168.30.50, mask 255.255.255.0. Enable DNS with record www.ccna.lab = 192.168.30.10. Confirm HTTP is On.
tasks.hi: Server1 > Services par DHCP enable karo: default gateway 192.168.30.10, DNS server 192.168.30.10, start IP 192.168.30.50, mask 255.255.255.0. DNS enable karo record www.ccna.lab = 192.168.30.10 ke saath. Confirm karo ki HTTP On hai.

tasks.en: Set PC1 to DHCP (Desktop > IP Configuration > DHCP), confirm it receives a .50+ address, then browse to http://www.ccna.lab.
tasks.hi: PC1 ko DHCP par set karo (Desktop > IP Configuration > DHCP), confirm karo ki use .50+ address milta hai, phir http://www.ccna.lab browse karo.

verify.en: PC1 IP Configuration — DHCP-assigned address in the 192.168.30.50+ range
verify.hi: PC1 IP Configuration — 192.168.30.50+ range mein DHCP-assigned address

verify.en: Web browser on PC1 — http://www.ccna.lab loads, proving DHCP, DNS and HTTP run on one host
verify.hi: PC1 par web browser — http://www.ccna.lab load hota hai, jo prove karta hai ki DHCP, DNS aur HTTP ek hi host par chal rahe hain

verify.en: Your table — 5 rows completed with kernel-sharing identified as the key container difference
verify.hi: Tumhari table — 5 rows complete, aur kernel-sharing ko container ka key difference identify kiya hua

verify.en: Your VRF definition — mentions separate routing tables on shared hardware
verify.hi: Tumhari VRF definition — shared hardware par alag routing tables ka zikr hai

note.en: Exam angle: know type-1 vs type-2 hypervisors, why containers start faster (no guest OS boot), and that a VRF virtualizes the routing table itself.
note.hi: Exam angle: type-1 vs type-2 hypervisors jaano, containers jaldi start kyun hote hain (guest OS boot nahi hota), aur yeh ki VRF khud routing table ko virtualize karta hai.

objective.en: Classify real scenarios into cloud service and deployment models and write a short cloud-managed networking migration note, producing an answer sheet you can self-check.
objective.hi: Real scenarios ko cloud service aur deployment models mein classify karo aur cloud-managed networking migration par ek chhota note likho, taaki ek answer sheet bane jise tum khud check kar sako.

topology: None — paper deliverables only (no Packet Tracer build today)

tasks.en: Write definitions in one line each: IaaS (you rent compute/storage/network, you manage OS and up), PaaS (you deploy code onto a managed platform), SaaS (you just use the finished application).
tasks.hi: Har ek ki definition ek line mein likho: IaaS (tum compute/storage/network rent karte ho, OS aur uske upar sab tum manage karte ho), PaaS (tum managed platform par apna code deploy karte ho), SaaS (tum bas ready application use karte ho).

tasks.en: Classify these six scenarios as IaaS, PaaS or SaaS: 1) Office 365 email, 2) an AWS EC2 virtual machine you patch yourself, 3) a managed database service where you only create tables, 4) Webex, 5) renting raw VMs to host your own CRM, 6) a serverless code platform. Write your answers before checking the verify section.
tasks.hi: In chhe scenarios ko IaaS, PaaS ya SaaS mein classify karo: 1) Office 365 email, 2) ek AWS EC2 virtual machine jise tum khud patch karte ho, 3) ek managed database service jahan tum sirf tables banate ho, 4) Webex, 5) apna CRM host karne ke liye raw VMs rent karna, 6) ek serverless code platform. Verify section check karne se pehle apne answers likh lo.

tasks.en: Classify deployment models: a hospital keeping patient systems in its own data center but bursting analytics to AWS (hybrid); a startup 100% on Azure (public); a bank running an internal OpenStack cloud (private); three universities sharing a research cloud (community).
tasks.hi: Deployment models classify karo: ek hospital jo patient systems apne data center mein rakhta hai lekin analytics ko AWS par burst karta hai (hybrid); ek startup jo 100% Azure par hai (public); ek bank jo internal OpenStack cloud chalata hai (private); teen universities jo ek research cloud share karti hain (community).

tasks.en: Write a 4-line comparison of on-prem vs cloud spending: CapEx vs OpEx, scaling speed, who maintains hardware, typical billing model.
tasks.hi: On-prem vs cloud spending ka 4-line comparison likho: CapEx vs OpEx, scaling speed, hardware kaun maintain karta hai, typical billing model.

tasks.en: Cloud-managed networking (v1.1 focus): in 5-6 sentences describe managing switches/APs through a cloud dashboard (e.g. Meraki-style): devices phone home over the internet, config is pushed from the cloud, telemetry and alerts are centralized, zero-touch provisioning replaces console cables. List one benefit (manage 100 sites from one browser) and one risk (dashboard reachability/subscription dependency).
tasks.hi: Cloud-managed networking (v1.1 focus): 5-6 sentences mein batao ki cloud dashboard se switches/APs kaise manage hote hain (jaise Meraki-style): devices internet par phone home karte hain, config cloud se push hota hai, telemetry aur alerts centralized hote hain, zero-touch provisioning console cables ki jagah le leta hai. Ek benefit (ek browser se 100 sites manage karna) aur ek risk (dashboard reachability/subscription dependency) list karo.

tasks.en: List the five NIST essential cloud characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service.
tasks.hi: Paanch NIST essential cloud characteristics list karo: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service.

tasks.en: File today's sheets with your subnetting tables — week 8 review will reuse them.
tasks.hi: Aaj ki sheets ko apni subnetting tables ke saath file kar do — week 8 review mein yeh dobara use hongi.

verify.en: Scenario answers — 1 SaaS, 2 IaaS, 3 PaaS, 4 SaaS, 5 IaaS, 6 PaaS
verify.hi: Scenario answers — 1 SaaS, 2 IaaS, 3 PaaS, 4 SaaS, 5 IaaS, 6 PaaS

verify.en: Deployment answers — hybrid, public, private, community
verify.hi: Deployment answers — hybrid, public, private, community

verify.en: NIST list — all five characteristics from memory
verify.hi: NIST list — paancho characteristics yaad se

note.en: Memory hook for service models: count what YOU still manage — everything above the hypervisor (IaaS), just your code and data (PaaS), nothing but your login (SaaS).
note.hi: Service models yaad rakhne ka tarika: gino ki TUM abhi bhi kya manage karte ho — hypervisor ke upar sab kuch (IaaS), sirf apna code aur data (PaaS), apne login ke alawa kuch nahi (SaaS).

title.hi: MAC Learning aur Tumhare Pehle VLANs

objective.en: Observe how one switch floods and learns, then segment it into two VLANs and prove that VLANs separate traffic even inside one subnet.
objective.hi: Dekho ek switch kaise flood karta hai aur seekhta hai, phir use do VLANs mein segment karo aur prove karo ki ek hi subnet ke andar bhi VLANs traffic ko alag karte hain.

tasks.en: Build the topology: one 2960 with four PCs. Address them all in one subnet: PC1 192.168.1.11, PC2 .12, PC3 .13, PC4 .14, mask 255.255.255.0 (no gateway).
tasks.hi: Topology banao: ek 2960 aur chaar PCs. Sabko ek hi subnet mein address do: PC1 192.168.1.11, PC2 .12, PC3 .13, PC4 .14, mask 255.255.255.0 (gateway nahi).

tasks.en: Ping from PC1 to each other PC — all succeed because every port is in default VLAN 1.
tasks.hi: PC1 se baaki har PC ko ping karo — sab succeed karte hain kyunki har port default VLAN 1 mein hai.

tasks.en: Run show mac address-table dynamic on SW1 and map all four MACs to their ports. Clear it with clear mac address-table dynamic and watch it repopulate after a ping.
tasks.hi: SW1 par show mac address-table dynamic chalao aur chaaron MACs ko unke ports se map karo. clear mac address-table dynamic se ise clear karo aur dekho ping ke baad yeh dobara bhar jati hai.

tasks.en: Create the VLANs: configure terminal, vlan 10, name Sales, exit, vlan 20, name HR, exit.
tasks.hi: VLANs banao: configure terminal, vlan 10, name Sales, exit, vlan 20, name HR, exit.

tasks.en: Assign ports to Sales: interface range f0/1 - 2, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 10, exit.
tasks.hi: Ports ko Sales mein daalo: interface range f0/1 - 2, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 10, exit.

tasks.en: Assign ports to HR: interface range f0/3 - 4, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 20, end.
tasks.hi: Ports ko HR mein daalo: interface range f0/3 - 4, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 20, end.

tasks.en: Run show vlan brief and confirm F0/1-2 sit under VLAN 10 and F0/3-4 under VLAN 20.
tasks.hi: show vlan brief chalao aur confirm karo ki F0/1-2 VLAN 10 ke neeche hain aur F0/3-4 VLAN 20 ke neeche.

tasks.en: Re-test: PC1 ping PC2 succeeds (same VLAN); PC1 ping PC3 now FAILS even though the IP subnet is identical — a VLAN is a separate broadcast domain and no router exists to cross it.
tasks.hi: Dobara test karo: PC1 se PC2 ping succeed hota hai (same VLAN); PC1 se PC3 ping ab FAIL hota hai jabki IP subnet bilkul same hai — VLAN ek alag broadcast domain hai aur use cross karne ke liye koi router nahi hai.

tasks.en: Run show mac address-table dynamic again and note each MAC is now learned inside its VLAN.
tasks.hi: show mac address-table dynamic phir se chalao aur note karo ki ab har MAC apne VLAN ke andar learn hua hai.

verify.en: show vlan brief — VLAN 10 Sales with F0/1-2, VLAN 20 HR with F0/3-4
verify.hi: show vlan brief — VLAN 10 Sales mein F0/1-2, VLAN 20 HR mein F0/3-4

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — success (intra-VLAN)
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — success (intra-VLAN)

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC3 — Request timed out (inter-VLAN with no router)
verify.hi: PC1 se PC3 ping — Request timed out (inter-VLAN, router nahi hai)

verify.en: show mac address-table dynamic — MACs listed under VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 respectively
verify.hi: show mac address-table dynamic — MACs apne-apne VLAN (VLAN 10 aur VLAN 20) ke neeche listed

note.en: Key mental model: a VLAN is a broadcast domain. Same subnet numbers mean nothing across VLANs — only a Layer 3 device can move traffic between them.
note.hi: Key mental model: VLAN ek broadcast domain hai. VLANs ke paar same subnet numbers ka koi matlab nahi — sirf ek Layer 3 device hi unke beech traffic le ja sakta hai.

objective.en: Extend VLANs 10 and 20 across two switches over a single 802.1Q trunk with a dedicated native VLAN and a pruned allowed list.
objective.hi: VLANs 10 aur 20 ko ek single 802.1Q trunk ke zariye do switches tak extend karo, ek dedicated native VLAN aur pruned allowed list ke saath.

topology: PC1 (F0/1, VLAN 10) and PC2 (F0/2, VLAN 20) — SW1 (G0/1) — (G0/1) SW2 — PC3 (F0/1, VLAN 10) and PC4 (F0/2, VLAN 20)

tasks.en: Build the topology: two 2960s linked G0/1-to-G0/1 (crossover cable), two PCs on each. Addresses: VLAN 10 PCs 192.168.10.11 and .13/24; VLAN 20 PCs 192.168.20.12 and .14/24.
tasks.hi: Topology banao: do 2960s G0/1-to-G0/1 linked (crossover cable), har ek par do PCs. Addresses: VLAN 10 PCs 192.168.10.11 aur .13/24; VLAN 20 PCs 192.168.20.12 aur .14/24.

tasks.en: On SW1 create the VLANs: vlan 10, name Sales, vlan 20, name HR, vlan 99, name Native, end. Repeat identically on SW2 (VLAN names must be created on both — VLANs are locally significant).
tasks.hi: SW1 par VLANs banao: vlan 10, name Sales, vlan 20, name HR, vlan 99, name Native, end. SW2 par bilkul same repeat karo (VLANs dono par banane padte hain — VLANs locally significant hote hain).

tasks.en: On both switches assign access ports: interface f0/1, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 10; interface f0/2, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 20.
tasks.hi: Dono switches par access ports assign karo: interface f0/1, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 10; interface f0/2, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 20.

tasks.en: Configure the trunk on SW1: interface g0/1, switchport mode trunk, switchport trunk native vlan 99, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,99.
tasks.hi: SW1 par trunk configure karo: interface g0/1, switchport mode trunk, switchport trunk native vlan 99, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,99.

tasks.en: Repeat the exact trunk config on SW2 g0/1. (Watch for the native-VLAN-mismatch CDP warning if you configure one side first — it disappears once both match.)
tasks.hi: SW2 g0/1 par exact same trunk config repeat karo. (Agar ek side pehle configure karte ho toh native-VLAN-mismatch CDP warning dikhegi — dono match hote hi woh gayab ho jati hai.)

tasks.en: Run show interfaces trunk on both switches: mode on, encapsulation 802.1q, native VLAN 99, allowed VLANs 10,20,99.
tasks.hi: Dono switches par show interfaces trunk chalao: mode on, encapsulation 802.1q, native VLAN 99, allowed VLANs 10,20,99.

tasks.en: Test: PC1 ping PC3 (VLAN 10 across the trunk — success). PC2 ping PC4 (VLAN 20 — success). PC1 ping PC4 — fails (different VLAN and different subnet, no router).
tasks.hi: Test: PC1 se PC3 ping (trunk ke paar VLAN 10 — success). PC2 se PC4 ping (VLAN 20 — success). PC1 se PC4 ping — fail (alag VLAN aur alag subnet, router nahi).

tasks.en: In Simulation mode filter ICMP only, ping PC1 to PC3, and click the frame while it crosses the trunk link — the PDU details show the 802.1Q header carrying VLAN ID 10.
tasks.hi: Simulation mode mein sirf ICMP filter karo, PC1 se PC3 ping karo, aur jab frame trunk link cross kar raha ho tab us par click karo — PDU details mein 802.1Q header VLAN ID 10 carry karta dikhega.

verify.en: show interfaces trunk — G0/1 trunking, native VLAN 99, allowed 10,20,99 on BOTH switches
verify.hi: show interfaces trunk — DONO switches par G0/1 trunking, native VLAN 99, allowed 10,20,99

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC3 and PC2 to PC4 — both succeed across the trunk
verify.hi: PC1 se PC3 aur PC2 se PC4 ping — dono trunk ke paar succeed

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC4 — fails as expected
verify.hi: PC1 se PC4 ping — expected tarah se fail

verify.en: Simulation PDU on the trunk link — dot1q tag with VLAN 10 visible
verify.hi: Trunk link par Simulation PDU — VLAN 10 wala dot1q tag dikhta hai

note.en: Best practice tested on the exam: change the native VLAN off VLAN 1, keep it unused by hosts, and prune the allowed list to only the VLANs you need.
note.hi: Exam mein test hone wali best practice: native VLAN ko VLAN 1 se hatao, use hosts ke liye unused rakho, aur allowed list ko sirf zaroori VLANs tak prune karo.

objective.en: Route between VLANs 10 and 20 using 802.1Q subinterfaces on a single router link.
objective.hi: Ek single router link par 802.1Q subinterfaces use karke VLANs 10 aur 20 ke beech route karo.

topology: PC1 (F0/1, VLAN 10) and PC2 (F0/2, VLAN 20) — SW1 (G0/1) — (G0/0) R1

tasks.en: On SW1 create VLANs 10 (Sales) and 20 (HR); make F0/1 an access port in VLAN 10 and F0/2 an access port in VLAN 20.
tasks.hi: SW1 par VLANs 10 (Sales) aur 20 (HR) banao; F0/1 ko VLAN 10 mein access port banao aur F0/2 ko VLAN 20 mein access port.

tasks.en: Make the switch uplink a trunk: interface g0/1, switchport mode trunk, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20.
tasks.hi: Switch uplink ko trunk banao: interface g0/1, switchport mode trunk, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20.

tasks.en: On R1 bring up the physical interface with NO address: interface g0/0, no shutdown.
tasks.hi: R1 par physical interface ko BINA address ke up karo: interface g0/0, no shutdown.

tasks.en: Create the VLAN 10 subinterface: interface g0/0.10, encapsulation dot1q 10, ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0.
tasks.hi: VLAN 10 subinterface banao: interface g0/0.10, encapsulation dot1q 10, ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0.

tasks.en: Create the VLAN 20 subinterface: interface g0/0.20, encapsulation dot1q 20, ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0, end.
tasks.hi: VLAN 20 subinterface banao: interface g0/0.20, encapsulation dot1q 20, ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0, end.

tasks.en: Confirm the router sees both networks: show ip route should list connected routes for 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24.
tasks.hi: Confirm karo ki router dono networks dekh raha hai: show ip route mein 192.168.10.0/24 aur 192.168.20.0/24 ke connected routes hone chahiye.

tasks.en: Test: PC1 ping 192.168.10.1 (own gateway), then ping 192.168.20.12 (PC2 — routed between VLANs over the single trunk).
tasks.hi: Test: PC1 se ping 192.168.10.1 (apna gateway), phir ping 192.168.20.12 (PC2 — single trunk par VLANs ke beech routed).

tasks.en: In Simulation mode watch the PC1-to-PC2 ping: the frame goes up the trunk tagged VLAN 10, into the router, and returns down the same physical link tagged VLAN 20.
tasks.hi: Simulation mode mein PC1-to-PC2 ping dekho: frame VLAN 10 tag ke saath trunk se upar jata hai, router mein jata hai, aur usi physical link se VLAN 20 tag ke saath wapas neeche aata hai.

verify.en: show interfaces trunk on SW1 — G0/1 trunking with VLANs 10,20 allowed
verify.hi: SW1 par show interfaces trunk — G0/1 trunking, VLANs 10,20 allowed

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — success through the router
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — router ke through success

verify.en: show ip interface brief on R1 — G0/0 up plus both subinterfaces up
verify.hi: R1 par show ip interface brief — G0/0 up aur dono subinterfaces bhi up

note.en: The three classic router-on-a-stick failures: encapsulation dot1q missing or wrong VLAN ID, switch uplink not trunking, or subinterface number confused with the VLAN ID (the number after the dot is cosmetic — the encapsulation command is what binds the VLAN).
note.hi: Router-on-a-stick ki teen classic failures: encapsulation dot1q missing ya galat VLAN ID, switch uplink trunking nahi kar raha, ya subinterface number ko VLAN ID samajh lena (dot ke baad wala number sirf cosmetic hai — VLAN ko encapsulation command hi bind karti hai).

title.en: Mapping a Network with CDP & LLDP
title.hi: CDP aur LLDP se Network Map banao

objective.en: Use CDP and LLDP outputs alone to draw an accurate topology map, then practice disabling discovery protocols where they leak information.
objective.hi: Sirf CDP aur LLDP outputs use karke ek accurate topology map draw karo, phir jahan discovery protocols information leak karte hain wahan unhe disable karne ki practice karo.

tasks.en: Build the topology (1941, two 2960s, one PC) and set hostnames R1, SW1, SW2. Bring R1 g0/0 up with no shutdown (no IP needed for CDP to work — it is Layer 2).
tasks.hi: Topology banao (1941, do 2960s, ek PC) aur hostnames R1, SW1, SW2 set karo. R1 g0/0 ko no shutdown se up karo (CDP ke kaam karne ke liye IP ki zaroorat nahi — yeh Layer 2 hai).

tasks.en: Wait about 60 seconds for advertisements, then on SW1 run show cdp neighbors. Read the columns: Device ID, Local Interface, Capability, Platform, Port ID (the NEIGHBOR'S port).
tasks.hi: Advertisements ke liye lagbhag 60 seconds ruko, phir SW1 par show cdp neighbors chalao. Columns padho: Device ID, Local Interface, Capability, Platform, Port ID (NEIGHBOR ka port).

tasks.en: Run show cdp neighbors detail on SW1 and note the extra data: IOS version and IP address of each neighbor — exactly why security policies often disable CDP.
tasks.hi: SW1 par show cdp neighbors detail chalao aur extra data note karo: har neighbor ka IOS version aur IP address — isi wajah se security policies aksar CDP disable karti hain.

tasks.en: Challenge: using only the CDP outputs from R1, SW1 and SW2 (no fair looking at the workspace), draw the full topology with every interface labeled. Compare with the actual build.
tasks.hi: Challenge: sirf R1, SW1 aur SW2 ke CDP outputs use karke (workspace dekhna allowed nahi), har interface label karke poora topology draw karo. Phir actual build se compare karo.

tasks.en: Enable LLDP everywhere (it is off by default on Cisco gear): on each device configure terminal, lldp run, end.
tasks.hi: Har jagah LLDP enable karo (Cisco gear par yeh default off hota hai): har device par configure terminal, lldp run, end.

tasks.en: After a minute run show lldp neighbors on SW1 and compare its table to CDP's (LLDP is the IEEE 802.1AB standard, so it also sees non-Cisco boxes; PCs may appear).
tasks.hi: Ek minute baad SW1 par show lldp neighbors chalao aur iski table ko CDP se compare karo (LLDP IEEE 802.1AB standard hai, isliye yeh non-Cisco boxes bhi dekhta hai; PCs bhi dikh sakte hain).

tasks.en: Disable CDP on just the PC-facing port (leak prevention): on SW2, interface f0/1, no cdp enable.
tasks.hi: Sirf PC-facing port par CDP disable karo (leak prevention): SW2 par interface f0/1, no cdp enable.

tasks.en: Disable CDP globally on R1 to see the difference in scope: no cdp run, then confirm SW1's CDP table ages R1 out (up to 180 seconds) while LLDP still shows it. Re-enable with cdp run.
tasks.hi: Scope ka fark dekhne ke liye R1 par CDP globally disable karo: no cdp run, phir confirm karo ki SW1 ki CDP table se R1 age out ho jata hai (180 seconds tak) jabki LLDP use abhi bhi dikhata hai. cdp run se dobara enable karo.

verify.en: show cdp neighbors on SW1 — two rows: R1 (capability R) and SW2 (capability S) with correct local and remote ports
verify.hi: SW1 par show cdp neighbors — do rows: R1 (capability R) aur SW2 (capability S), sahi local aur remote ports ke saath

verify.en: show lldp neighbors on SW1 — same devices learned via the open standard
verify.hi: SW1 par show lldp neighbors — wahi devices open standard se learn hue

verify.en: Your hand-drawn map — matches the real topology interface-for-interface
verify.hi: Tumhara haath se bana map — real topology se interface-for-interface match karta hai

verify.en: show cdp neighbors on SW1 after no cdp run on R1 — R1 entry gone after the holdtime expires
verify.hi: R1 par no cdp run ke baad SW1 par show cdp neighbors — holdtime expire hone ke baad R1 ki entry gayab

note.en: Interface scope: no cdp enable (interface) vs no cdp run (global). CDP timers: advertisements every 60 s, holdtime 180 s. LLDP equivalents exist per-interface as lldp transmit / lldp receive.
note.hi: Interface scope: no cdp enable (interface) vs no cdp run (global). CDP timers: advertisements har 60 s, holdtime 180 s. LLDP ke equivalent per-interface lldp transmit / lldp receive hain.

objective.en: Bundle two links between switches into one logical LACP port channel carrying a trunk, then verify the bundle and observe what a mode mismatch does.
objective.hi: Switches ke beech do links ko ek logical LACP port channel mein bundle karo jo trunk carry kare, phir bundle verify karo aur dekho mode mismatch kya karta hai.

tasks.en: Build the topology: two 2960s connected by TWO crossover cables (F0/1-F0/1 and F0/2-F0/2), one PC on each switch (PC1 192.168.1.11/24, PC2 192.168.1.12/24).
tasks.hi: Topology banao: do 2960s DO crossover cables se connected (F0/1-F0/1 aur F0/2-F0/2), har switch par ek PC (PC1 192.168.1.11/24, PC2 192.168.1.12/24).

tasks.en: Notice spanning tree has already blocked one of the two parallel links (amber light) — the problem EtherChannel solves.
tasks.hi: Dhyan do ki spanning tree ne do parallel links mein se ek ko pehle hi block kar diya hai (amber light) — yahi problem EtherChannel solve karta hai.

tasks.en: On SW1 bundle the links with LACP: interface range f0/1 - 2, channel-group 1 mode active, exit. IOS creates interface Port-channel1 automatically.
tasks.hi: SW1 par LACP se links bundle karo: interface range f0/1 - 2, channel-group 1 mode active, exit. IOS apne aap interface Port-channel1 bana deta hai.

tasks.en: On SW2: interface range f0/1 - 2, channel-group 1 mode passive, exit. (active+passive or active+active both form LACP bundles.)
tasks.hi: SW2 par: interface range f0/1 - 2, channel-group 1 mode passive, exit. (active+passive ya active+active dono LACP bundle bana dete hain.)

tasks.en: Configure the logical interface as a trunk on both switches: interface port-channel 1, switchport mode trunk.
tasks.hi: Dono switches par logical interface ko trunk configure karo: interface port-channel 1, switchport mode trunk.

tasks.en: Run show etherchannel summary on both sides: look for Po1(SU) — S means Layer 2, U means in use — with (P) beside both member ports.
tasks.hi: Dono sides par show etherchannel summary chalao: Po1(SU) dhoondo — S matlab Layer 2, U matlab in use — aur dono member ports ke bagal mein (P).

tasks.en: Both physical links should now show green: STP sees one logical link, so nothing is blocked. Confirm PC1 can ping PC2.
tasks.hi: Ab dono physical links green dikhne chahiye: STP ek hi logical link dekhta hai, isliye kuch block nahi hota. Confirm karo ki PC1, PC2 ko ping kar sakta hai.

tasks.en: Break it deliberately: on SW2, interface range f0/1 - 2, no channel-group 1, then channel-group 1 mode on (static, no protocol). Re-run show etherchannel summary on SW1 — the bundle goes down (SD or ports in standalone) because 'on' does not negotiate with LACP active. Restore mode passive and re-verify SU.
tasks.hi: Jaan-boojh kar todo: SW2 par interface range f0/1 - 2, no channel-group 1, phir channel-group 1 mode on (static, koi protocol nahi). SW1 par show etherchannel summary dobara chalao — bundle down ho jata hai (SD ya ports standalone) kyunki 'on' LACP active ke saath negotiate nahi karta. mode passive restore karo aur SU dobara verify karo.

verify.en: show etherchannel summary — Flags Po1(SU), member ports F0/1(P) F0/2(P) on both switches
verify.hi: show etherchannel summary — dono switches par Flags Po1(SU), member ports F0/1(P) F0/2(P)

verify.en: show interfaces trunk — Po1 listed as the trunking interface (not the physical ports)
verify.hi: show interfaces trunk — trunking interface ke roop mein Po1 listed hai (physical ports nahi)

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — success across the bundle
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — bundle ke paar success

verify.en: After the mode-on mismatch — Po1 no longer SU, proving on+active is incompatible
verify.hi: mode-on mismatch ke baad — Po1 ab SU nahi hai, jo prove karta hai ki on+active incompatible hai

note.en: Mode pairs that work — LACP: active+active, active+passive. PAgP: desirable+desirable, desirable+auto. Static: on+on only. Never mix protocols or mix 'on' with a negotiating mode.
note.hi: Kaam karne wale mode pairs — LACP: active+active, active+passive. PAgP: desirable+desirable, desirable+auto. Static: sirf on+on. Protocols ko kabhi mix mat karo, aur 'on' ko kisi negotiating mode ke saath mix mat karo.

objective.en: Build a known-good two-switch network, inject three classic Layer 2 faults, and repair each using a fixed top-down command workflow.
objective.hi: Ek known-good two-switch network banao, usme teen classic Layer 2 faults daalo, aur har ek ko ek fixed top-down command workflow se repair karo.

topology: PC1 (F0/10, VLAN 10) — SW1 (F0/1, F0/2 = Po1 trunk) — SW2 (F0/10, VLAN 10) — PC3; SW1 (F0/11, VLAN 20) — PC2; SW2 (F0/11, VLAN 20) — PC4

tasks.en: Build the baseline from memory (this rehearses labs 13, 14 and 17): VLANs 10 and 20 on both switches, access ports as in the topology, PC addressing 192.168.10.x/24 for VLAN 10 and 192.168.20.x/24 for VLAN 20, and a 2-link LACP EtherChannel (channel-group 1 mode active both sides) trunking VLANs 10 and 20.
tasks.hi: Baseline yaad se banao (isse labs 13, 14 aur 17 ki practice hoti hai): dono switches par VLANs 10 aur 20, access ports topology ke hisaab se, VLAN 10 ke liye PC addressing 192.168.10.x/24 aur VLAN 20 ke liye 192.168.20.x/24, aur ek 2-link LACP EtherChannel (dono sides channel-group 1 mode active) jo VLANs 10 aur 20 trunk kare.

tasks.en: Prove the baseline: PC1 ping PC3 and PC2 ping PC4 both succeed. Save configs on both switches.
tasks.hi: Baseline prove karo: PC1 se PC3 ping aur PC2 se PC4 ping dono succeed hone chahiye. Dono switches par configs save karo.

tasks.en: Memorize the workflow you will use for every fault: 1 show vlan brief (are ports in the right VLANs?), 2 show interfaces trunk (is the trunk up and are the VLANs allowed?), 3 show etherchannel summary (is the bundle SU?), 4 show mac address-table (is the switch learning?).
tasks.hi: Har fault ke liye use hone wala workflow yaad karo: 1 show vlan brief (kya ports sahi VLANs mein hain?), 2 show interfaces trunk (kya trunk up hai aur VLANs allowed hain?), 3 show etherchannel summary (kya bundle SU hai?), 4 show mac address-table (kya switch seekh raha hai?).

tasks.en: Fault 1: on SW2, interface f0/10, switchport access vlan 30 (wrong VLAN). Run the workflow — show vlan brief exposes it. Fix with switchport access vlan 10 and confirm PC1 can ping PC3 again.
tasks.hi: Fault 1: SW2 par interface f0/10, switchport access vlan 30 (galat VLAN). Workflow chalao — show vlan brief ise pakad leta hai. switchport access vlan 10 se fix karo aur confirm karo ki PC1 phir se PC3 ko ping kar sakta hai.

tasks.en: Fault 2: on SW1, interface port-channel 1, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10 (VLAN 20 pruned). PC2 to PC4 dies while PC1 to PC3 still works — that asymmetry is the clue. show interfaces trunk exposes the missing VLAN. Fix with switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20.
tasks.hi: Fault 2: SW1 par interface port-channel 1, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10 (VLAN 20 pruned). PC2 se PC4 band ho jata hai jabki PC1 se PC3 abhi bhi chalta hai — yahi asymmetry clue hai. show interfaces trunk missing VLAN dikha deta hai. switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20 se fix karo.

tasks.en: Fault 3: on SW2, interface range f0/1 - 2, no channel-group 1, then channel-group 1 mode on. show etherchannel summary shows the broken bundle. Fix by restoring channel-group 1 mode active (remove the 'on' config first).
tasks.hi: Fault 3: SW2 par interface range f0/1 - 2, no channel-group 1, phir channel-group 1 mode on. show etherchannel summary toota hua bundle dikhata hai. channel-group 1 mode active restore karke fix karo (pehle 'on' wala config hatao).

tasks.en: After each fix, re-run both test pings before moving on — never stack unverified fixes.
tasks.hi: Har fix ke baad aage badhne se pehle dono test pings dobara chalao — bina verify kiye fixes kabhi stack mat karo.

tasks.en: Write the four-step workflow on a card; you will reuse it in the week 8 super labs.
tasks.hi: Chaar-step workflow ek card par likh lo; week 8 ke super labs mein yeh dobara kaam aayega.

verify.en: Baseline and after every fix — PC1 to PC3 and PC2 to PC4 pings both succeed
verify.hi: Baseline aur har fix ke baad — PC1 se PC3 aur PC2 se PC4 dono pings succeed

verify.en: show vlan brief — every access port in its intended VLAN
verify.hi: show vlan brief — har access port apne intended VLAN mein

verify.en: show interfaces trunk — Po1 trunking with VLANs 10,20 allowed
verify.hi: show interfaces trunk — Po1 trunking, VLANs 10,20 allowed

verify.en: show etherchannel summary — Po1(SU) with both members (P)
verify.hi: show etherchannel summary — Po1(SU), dono members (P)

note.en: Troubleshooting discipline: change one thing, re-test, then move on. The asymmetric failure in fault 2 (one VLAN works, one does not) always points at the allowed-VLAN list.
note.hi: Troubleshooting discipline: ek cheez badlo, re-test karo, phir aage badho. Fault 2 jaisi asymmetric failure (ek VLAN chalta hai, ek nahi) hamesha allowed-VLAN list ki taraf ishara karti hai.

objective.en: Build a switching triangle, identify the elected root bridge and the blocked port, and watch STP reconverge when a link dies.
objective.hi: Ek switching triangle banao, elected root bridge aur blocked port pehchano, aur dekho link down hone par STP kaise reconverge karta hai.

tasks.en: Build the triangle with three 2960s (crossover cables between switches) and one PC on SW2 and SW3 (192.168.1.11 and .12/24).
tasks.hi: Teen 2960s se triangle banao (switches ke beech crossover cables) aur SW2 aur SW3 par ek-ek PC (192.168.1.11 aur .12/24).

tasks.en: Wait for convergence (about 30-50 seconds) — one inter-switch port shows an amber light: STP has blocked it to break the physical loop.
tasks.hi: Convergence ka wait karo (lagbhag 30-50 seconds) — ek inter-switch port amber light dikhata hai: physical loop todne ke liye STP ne use block kar diya hai.

tasks.en: Run show spanning-tree on SW1. Read the top block: Root ID (priority and MAC of the ROOT bridge) versus Bridge ID (this switch). If they match, the output also says 'This bridge is the root'.
tasks.hi: SW1 par show spanning-tree chalao. Upar wala block padho: Root ID (ROOT bridge ki priority aur MAC) vs Bridge ID (yeh switch). Agar dono match karte hain toh output mein 'This bridge is the root' bhi likha hota hai.

tasks.en: Run show spanning-tree on all three switches and identify the root. All priorities are the default 32769 (32768 plus VLAN 1), so the LOWEST MAC address wins. Write down the election result.
tasks.hi: Teeno switches par show spanning-tree chalao aur root pehchano. Sab priorities default 32769 hain (32768 plus VLAN 1), isliye sabse KAM MAC address jeetta hai. Election ka result likh lo.

tasks.en: On each non-root switch identify the root port (role Root, the lowest-cost path toward the root) and on exactly one switch find the blocked port (role Altn, status BLK).
tasks.hi: Har non-root switch par root port pehchano (role Root, root ki taraf lowest-cost path) aur theek ek switch par blocked port dhoondo (role Altn, status BLK).

tasks.en: Sketch the triangle on paper and mark: root bridge, root ports, designated ports, blocked port. Every link must have a designated port on one end.
tasks.hi: Paper par triangle sketch karo aur mark karo: root bridge, root ports, designated ports, blocked port. Har link ke ek end par designated port hona hi chahiye.

tasks.en: Confirm PC1 can ping PC2, then start a repeating ping and delete the cable currently carrying traffic between the two PC switches. Watch the amber (blocked) port turn green as STP unblocks it — the pings resume after the reconvergence pause.
tasks.hi: Confirm karo ki PC1, PC2 ko ping kar sakta hai, phir ek repeating ping start karo aur jo cable abhi dono PC switches ke beech traffic le ja raha hai use delete karo. Dekho amber (blocked) port green ho jata hai jab STP use unblock karta hai — reconvergence pause ke baad pings wapas chalne lagte hain.

tasks.en: Re-run show spanning-tree and compare port roles to your sketch.
tasks.hi: show spanning-tree dobara chalao aur port roles ko apne sketch se compare karo.

verify.en: show spanning-tree — exactly one switch reports 'This bridge is the root'
verify.hi: show spanning-tree — theek ek switch 'This bridge is the root' report karta hai

verify.en: show spanning-tree on the non-root switches — one port role Altn with status BLK somewhere in the triangle
verify.hi: non-root switches par show spanning-tree — triangle mein kahin ek port role Altn status BLK ke saath

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — recovers after the link is deleted and STP unblocks the alternate path
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — link delete hone aur STP ke alternate path unblock karne ke baad recover ho jata hai

verify.en: Your sketch — root, root ports, designated ports and the blocked port all labeled consistently
verify.hi: Tumhara sketch — root, root ports, designated ports aur blocked port sab consistently labeled

note.en: Election tiebreak order: lowest bridge priority, then lowest MAC. Default priority 32768 plus the VLAN ID means VLAN 1 shows 32769. Never let an old access switch with a low MAC accidentally be your root.
note.hi: Election tiebreak order: sabse kam bridge priority, phir sabse kam MAC. Default priority 32768 plus VLAN ID, isliye VLAN 1 mein 32769 dikhta hai. Kabhi kisi purane access switch ko, jiska MAC kam hai, galti se apna root mat banne do.

title.en: Root Control, Rapid PVST+, PortFast & BPDU Guard
title.hi: Root Control, Rapid PVST+, PortFast aur BPDU Guard

objective.en: Force the root bridge to a switch of your choosing, migrate to Rapid PVST+, and protect access ports with PortFast plus BPDU Guard.
objective.hi: Root bridge ko apni marzi ke switch par force karo, Rapid PVST+ par migrate karo, aur access ports ko PortFast plus BPDU Guard se protect karo.

topology: SW1 (G0/1) — (G0/1) SW2; SW2 (G0/2) — (G0/2) SW3; SW3 (G0/1) — (G0/2) SW1; PC1 — SW1 (F0/1); SW-Rogue (spare switch, initially unplugged)

tasks.en: Rebuild (or reuse) the lab-19 triangle. Run show spanning-tree and note which switch is currently root by MAC-address luck.
tasks.hi: lab-19 wala triangle dobara banao (ya reuse karo). show spanning-tree chalao aur note karo ki abhi MAC-address luck se kaunsa switch root hai.

tasks.en: Make SW1 the deterministic root for VLAN 1: on SW1, spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 24576. Re-run show spanning-tree on SW1 — it should now say 'This bridge is the root'. (Priorities must be multiples of 4096.)
tasks.hi: SW1 ko VLAN 1 ka deterministic root banao: SW1 par spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 24576. SW1 par show spanning-tree dobara chalao — ab 'This bridge is the root' aana chahiye. (Priorities 4096 ke multiples hone chahiye.)

tasks.en: Make SW2 the backup root: spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 28672. Verify the blocked port moved to SW3's side of the triangle as topology recalculates.
tasks.hi: SW2 ko backup root banao: spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 28672. Topology recalculate hone par verify karo ki blocked port triangle mein SW3 ki side chala gaya.

tasks.en: Migrate all three switches to Rapid PVST+: on each, spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst. Run show spanning-tree and confirm the protocol line now reads rstp.
tasks.hi: Teeno switches ko Rapid PVST+ par migrate karo: har ek par spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst. show spanning-tree chalao aur confirm karo ki protocol line ab rstp padhti hai.

tasks.en: On SW1's PC port enable PortFast so hosts skip listening/learning: interface f0/1, spanning-tree portfast (read the warning IOS prints — PortFast belongs on HOST ports only).
tasks.hi: SW1 ke PC port par PortFast enable karo taaki hosts listening/learning skip kar dein: interface f0/1, spanning-tree portfast (IOS jo warning print karta hai use padho — PortFast sirf HOST ports par hi lagta hai).

tasks.en: Arm the port against rogue switches: still on f0/1, spanning-tree bpduguard enable, end.
tasks.hi: Port ko rogue switches ke against arm karo: f0/1 par hi rehte hue, spanning-tree bpduguard enable, end.

tasks.en: Test the guard: disconnect PC1 and cable the spare switch SW-Rogue into SW1 F0/1. The rogue's BPDUs trip the guard — the port goes err-disabled (link light red/down).
tasks.hi: Guard test karo: PC1 disconnect karo aur spare switch SW-Rogue ko SW1 F0/1 mein cable karo. Rogue ke BPDUs guard ko trip kar dete hain — port err-disabled ho jata hai (link light red/down).

tasks.en: Inspect the damage with show interfaces status (f0/1 shows err-disabled). Recover: remove the rogue, reconnect PC1, then on SW1 interface f0/1 do shutdown followed by no shutdown.
tasks.hi: show interfaces status se damage dekho (f0/1 err-disabled dikhata hai). Recover karo: rogue hatao, PC1 dobara connect karo, phir SW1 par interface f0/1 mein shutdown aur uske baad no shutdown karo.

tasks.en: Bounce PC1's port (shutdown / no shutdown) and watch it jump to forwarding almost instantly thanks to PortFast plus RSTP.
tasks.hi: PC1 ka port bounce karo (shutdown / no shutdown) aur dekho PortFast plus RSTP ki wajah se woh lagbhag turant forwarding mein pahunch jata hai.

verify.en: show spanning-tree on SW1 — priority 24576 and 'This bridge is the root'
verify.hi: SW1 par show spanning-tree — priority 24576 aur 'This bridge is the root'

verify.en: show spanning-tree — protocol rstp on all three switches
verify.hi: show spanning-tree — teeno switches par protocol rstp

verify.en: show interfaces status after the rogue test — F0/1 err-disabled
verify.hi: rogue test ke baad show interfaces status — F0/1 err-disabled

verify.en: show spanning-tree interface f0/1 portfast — PortFast enabled (after recovery)
verify.hi: show spanning-tree interface f0/1 portfast — PortFast enabled (recovery ke baad)

note.en: Alternative root command: spanning-tree vlan 1 root primary picks a priority for you, but the exam expects you to know the manual priority multiples of 4096 too.
note.hi: Alternative root command: spanning-tree vlan 1 root primary tumhare liye priority khud chun leta hai, lekin exam expect karta hai ki tum 4096 ke multiples wali manual priority bhi jaano.

title.en: Wireless Principles with a Home AP
title.hi: Home AP ke saath Wireless Principles

objective.en: Stand up a small 2.4 GHz wireless LAN, associate laptops to it, and apply the non-overlapping channel rule.
objective.hi: Ek chhota 2.4 GHz wireless LAN khada karo, laptops ko usse associate karo, aur non-overlapping channel rule apply karo.

topology: WRT300N (Ethernet 1) — (F0/1) SW1 (F0/2) — PC1 (wired admin); Laptop1 and Laptop2 associate over wireless

tasks.en: Place a WRT300N home wireless router, a 2960, one PC and two Laptops. Cable WRT300N Ethernet 1 to SW1 F0/1 and PC1 to SW1 F0/2.
tasks.hi: Ek WRT300N home wireless router, ek 2960, ek PC aur do Laptops rakho. WRT300N Ethernet 1 ko SW1 F0/1 se aur PC1 ko SW1 F0/2 se cable karo.

tasks.en: Give the laptops wireless NICs: click Laptop1 > Physical tab, power it off (button on the chassis), drag the Ethernet module out of its bay, drag in the WPC300N wireless module, power back on. Repeat for Laptop2.
tasks.hi: Laptops ko wireless NICs do: Laptop1 > Physical tab par click karo, use power off karo (chassis par button), Ethernet module ko bay se bahar drag karo, WPC300N wireless module andar drag karo, phir power on karo. Laptop2 ke liye repeat karo.

tasks.en: Admin PC setup: PC1 to DHCP — it should pull a 192.168.0.x address from the WRT300N. Open Desktop > Web Browser to http://192.168.0.1 (login admin / admin).
tasks.hi: Admin PC setup: PC1 ko DHCP par rakho — use WRT300N se 192.168.0.x address milna chahiye. Desktop > Web Browser se http://192.168.0.1 kholo (login admin / admin).
