tasks.en: In the GUI go to Wireless > Basic Wireless Settings: SSID CCNA-Home, standard channel 6 - 2.437GHz. Save Settings.
tasks.hi: GUI mein Wireless > Basic Wireless Settings par jao: SSID CCNA-Home, standard channel 6 - 2.437GHz. Save Settings karo.

tasks.en: Associate Laptop1: Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect tab, refresh, select CCNA-Home, Connect. Check Desktop > IP Configuration shows a DHCP address from 192.168.0.0/24.
tasks.hi: Laptop1 associate karo: Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect tab, refresh, CCNA-Home select karo, Connect. Check karo ki Desktop > IP Configuration mein 192.168.0.0/24 se DHCP address dikh raha hai.

tasks.en: Associate Laptop2 the same way, then ping Laptop1's address from Laptop2 — traffic flows through the AP.
tasks.hi: Laptop2 ko bhi isi tarah associate karo, phir Laptop2 se Laptop1 ke address ko ping karo — traffic AP ke through jata hai.

tasks.en: Channel experiment: in the GUI change the channel to 1 - 2.412GHz and save. Watch the laptops briefly drop and re-associate on the new channel.
tasks.hi: Channel experiment: GUI mein channel ko 1 - 2.412GHz kar do aur save karo. Dekho laptops thodi der ke liye drop hote hain aur naye channel par re-associate hote hain.

tasks.en: On paper: draw the 2.4 GHz band and mark why only channels 1, 6 and 11 are non-overlapping (each channel is about 22 MHz wide, spaced 5 MHz apart). Then map standards to bands: 802.11b/g/n = 2.4 GHz, 802.11a/n/ac = 5 GHz, 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) = both.
tasks.hi: Paper par: 2.4 GHz band draw karo aur mark karo ki sirf channels 1, 6 aur 11 hi non-overlapping kyun hain (har channel lagbhag 22 MHz wide hai, aur 5 MHz ki doori par hain). Phir standards ko bands se map karo: 802.11b/g/n = 2.4 GHz, 802.11a/n/ac = 5 GHz, 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) = dono.

tasks.en: Also note the AP's BSSID concept: the radio's MAC identifies the BSS; the SSID CCNA-Home is just the human-readable name.
tasks.hi: AP ka BSSID concept bhi note karo: radio ka MAC BSS ko identify karta hai; SSID CCNA-Home bas human-readable naam hai.

verify.en: PC Wireless on both laptops — associated to SSID CCNA-Home with signal shown
verify.hi: Dono laptops par PC Wireless — SSID CCNA-Home se associated, signal dikh raha hai

verify.en: ping Laptop1 from Laptop2 — success through the AP
verify.hi: Laptop2 se Laptop1 ko ping — AP ke through success

verify.en: Your channel sketch — 1, 6, 11 marked non-overlapping in 2.4 GHz
verify.hi: Tumhara channel sketch — 2.4 GHz mein 1, 6, 11 non-overlapping marked

verify.en: Standards table — b/g in 2.4, a/ac in 5, n and ax in both bands
verify.hi: Standards table — b/g 2.4 mein, a/ac 5 mein, n aur ax dono bands mein

note.en: Adjacent-channel interference (channels 2-5 overlapping 1 and 6) is worse than co-channel contention — that is why real deployments reuse only 1, 6 and 11 in 2.4 GHz.
note.hi: Adjacent-channel interference (channels 2-5 jo 1 aur 6 se overlap karte hain) co-channel contention se zyada bura hai — isi wajah se real deployments 2.4 GHz mein sirf 1, 6 aur 11 reuse karte hain.

title.hi: WLC aur Lightweight APs ka Join

objective.en: Deploy a 3504 Wireless LAN Controller with two lightweight APs, provide DHCP so the APs can discover the controller, and confirm CAPWAP joins.
objective.hi: Do lightweight APs ke saath ek 3504 Wireless LAN Controller deploy karo, DHCP do taaki APs controller ko discover kar sakein, aur confirm karo ki CAPWAP join ho gaya.

topology: WLC1 (3504, G1) — (G0/1) SW1; LAP1 (G0) — (F0/1) SW1; LAP2 (G0) — (F0/2) SW1; Server1 (DHCP, Fa0) — (F0/3) SW1; Admin-PC (Fa0) — (F0/4) SW1

tasks.en: Place a 3504 WLC, two Lightweight Access Points (LAP-PT), a 2960, a Server-PT and an admin PC. Cable everything to SW1 as in the topology (all one flat subnet for this lab).
tasks.hi: Ek 3504 WLC, do Lightweight Access Points (LAP-PT), ek 2960, ek Server-PT aur ek admin PC rakho. Topology ke hisaab se sab kuch SW1 se cable karo (is lab mein sab ek hi flat subnet mein hai).

tasks.en: Configure Server1 statically: 192.168.200.10, mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.200.1. Turn its DHCP service On: default gateway 192.168.200.1, start IP 192.168.200.100, mask 255.255.255.0, plenty of addresses (the APs and later the clients will use this pool).
tasks.hi: Server1 ko statically configure karo: 192.168.200.10, mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.200.1. Uski DHCP service On karo: default gateway 192.168.200.1, start IP 192.168.200.100, mask 255.255.255.0, kaafi saare addresses (APs aur baad mein clients yahi pool use karenge).

tasks.en: Set the WLC management address: click WLC1 > Config tab > Management, set IP 192.168.200.5, mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.200.1.
tasks.hi: WLC ka management address set karo: WLC1 > Config tab > Management par click karo, IP 192.168.200.5, mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.200.1 set karo.

tasks.en: Set Admin-PC to static 192.168.200.50/24 (same subnet as the WLC management interface).
tasks.hi: Admin-PC ko static 192.168.200.50/24 par set karo (WLC management interface wala hi subnet).

tasks.en: From Admin-PC open Desktop > Web Browser to https://192.168.200.5 and complete the WLC first-time setup, creating admin user admin with password Cisco123! (Packet Tracer walks you through the wizard on first login).
tasks.hi: Admin-PC se Desktop > Web Browser mein https://192.168.200.5 kholo aur WLC first-time setup poora karo, admin user admin password Cisco123! ke saath banao (first login par Packet Tracer tumhe wizard se guide karta hai).

tasks.en: Watch the LAPs: they power up, take DHCP addresses from Server1, then discover the WLC via broadcast on the shared subnet and build CAPWAP tunnels. This can take a minute or two of simulation time.
tasks.hi: LAPs ko dekho: woh power up hote hain, Server1 se DHCP addresses lete hain, phir shared subnet par broadcast se WLC ko discover karte hain aur CAPWAP tunnels banate hain. Isme simulation time ke ek-do minute lag sakte hain.

tasks.en: In the WLC GUI go to Wireless (or Monitor > Access Points) and confirm both LAPs are listed as joined, each with its DHCP address.
tasks.hi: WLC GUI mein Wireless (ya Monitor > Access Points) par jao aur confirm karo ki dono LAPs joined listed hain, har ek apne DHCP address ke saath.

tasks.en: On paper, contrast this with lab-21: autonomous AP (all config on the box) vs lightweight AP (config lives on the WLC, AP tunnels traffic/control via CAPWAP — control UDP 5246, data UDP 5247). Note split-MAC: real-time 802.11 functions stay on the AP, management functions move to the WLC.
tasks.hi: Paper par ise lab-21 se contrast karo: autonomous AP (saara config box par hi) vs lightweight AP (config WLC par rehta hai, AP traffic/control ko CAPWAP se tunnel karta hai — control UDP 5246, data UDP 5247). Split-MAC note karo: real-time 802.11 functions AP par rehte hain, management functions WLC par chale jaate hain.

verify.en: WLC GUI Wireless page — both LAPs listed with operational status joined/registered
verify.hi: WLC GUI Wireless page — dono LAPs operational status joined/registered ke saath listed

verify.en: Server1 DHCP service — leases handed to both APs (addresses in the .100+ range)
verify.hi: Server1 DHCP service — dono APs ko leases diye gaye (.100+ range mein addresses)

verify.en: https://192.168.200.5 from Admin-PC — WLC dashboard loads and login works
verify.hi: Admin-PC se https://192.168.200.5 — WLC dashboard load hota hai aur login kaam karta hai

verify.en: Paper notes — CAPWAP ports UDP 5246 (control) and 5247 (data) recorded
verify.hi: Paper notes — CAPWAP ports UDP 5246 (control) aur 5247 (data) likhe hue

note.en: Lightweight APs cannot serve clients without a controller. In production, APs find WLCs via DHCP option 43, DNS or broadcast — Packet Tracer uses the same-subnet broadcast method.
note.hi: Lightweight APs controller ke bina clients ko serve nahi kar sakte. Production mein APs WLCs ko DHCP option 43, DNS ya broadcast se dhoondte hain — Packet Tracer same-subnet broadcast method use karta hai.

title.en: Build a WPA2 WLAN on the WLC

objective.en: Create a WPA2-PSK WLAN on the 3504 controller and connect a wireless laptop through the lightweight APs with a DHCP address.
objective.hi: 3504 controller par ek WPA2-PSK WLAN banao aur ek wireless laptop ko lightweight APs ke through DHCP address ke saath connect karo.

topology: Same as lab-22: WLC1 + LAP1 + LAP2 + Server1 + Admin-PC on SW1; Laptop1 joins over wireless

tasks.en: Reopen your lab-22 file (both APs must show as joined before starting).
tasks.hi: Apni lab-22 file dobara kholo (start karne se pehle dono APs joined dikhne chahiye).

tasks.en: From Admin-PC log in to https://192.168.200.5. Go to WLANs > Create New > Go.
tasks.hi: Admin-PC se https://192.168.200.5 par log in karo. WLANs > Create New > Go par jao.

tasks.en: Set Profile Name CCNA-Corp and SSID CCNA-Corp, then Apply. On the WLAN's General tab check Status Enabled and leave the interface as management for this flat-network lab.
tasks.hi: Profile Name CCNA-Corp aur SSID CCNA-Corp set karo, phir Apply. WLAN ke General tab par Status Enabled check karo aur is flat-network lab ke liye interface ko management hi rehne do.

tasks.en: Open the Security > Layer 2 tab: Layer 2 Security WPA+WPA2, tick WPA2 Policy and AES, Auth Key Mgmt PSK, and set passphrase StudyHard88. Apply, then Save Configuration.
tasks.hi: Security > Layer 2 tab kholo: Layer 2 Security WPA+WPA2, WPA2 Policy aur AES tick karo, Auth Key Mgmt PSK, aur passphrase StudyHard88 set karo. Apply karo, phir Save Configuration.

tasks.en: Prepare Laptop1: swap in the WPC300N wireless module (power off, swap, power on) as you did in lab-21.
tasks.hi: Laptop1 taiyaar karo: WPC300N wireless module swap karo (power off, swap, power on) jaise lab-21 mein kiya tha.

tasks.en: On Laptop1 open Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect, refresh until CCNA-Corp appears, select it, enter the WPA2 passphrase StudyHard88 and connect.
tasks.hi: Laptop1 par Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect kholo, tab tak refresh karo jab tak CCNA-Corp na dikhe, use select karo, WPA2 passphrase StudyHard88 daalo aur connect karo.

tasks.en: Confirm Laptop1 pulled a DHCP address from Server1's pool (Desktop > IP Configuration).
tasks.hi: Confirm karo ki Laptop1 ne Server1 ke pool se DHCP address liya (Desktop > IP Configuration).

tasks.en: From Laptop1 ping 192.168.200.10 (the server) and 192.168.200.5 (the WLC management IP).
tasks.hi: Laptop1 se 192.168.200.10 (server) aur 192.168.200.5 (WLC management IP) ko ping karo.

tasks.en: Walk to the other AP: drag Laptop1 across the workspace near LAP2 — in Packet Tracer's physical workspace the laptop can re-associate, illustrating that both APs broadcast the same WLAN from one controller config.
tasks.hi: Doosre AP tak jao: Laptop1 ko workspace mein drag karke LAP2 ke paas le jao — Packet Tracer ke physical workspace mein laptop re-associate kar sakta hai, jisse dikhta hai ki dono APs ek hi controller config se same WLAN broadcast karte hain.

verify.en: WLC GUI WLANs page — CCNA-Corp enabled with WPA2/AES PSK security
verify.hi: WLC GUI WLANs page — CCNA-Corp enabled, WPA2/AES PSK security ke saath

verify.en: PC Wireless on Laptop1 — associated to CCNA-Corp
verify.hi: Laptop1 par PC Wireless — CCNA-Corp se associated

verify.en: Laptop1 IP Configuration — DHCP address from 192.168.200.100+
verify.hi: Laptop1 IP Configuration — 192.168.200.100+ se DHCP address

verify.en: ping 192.168.200.10 from Laptop1 — success end to end through CAPWAP
verify.hi: Laptop1 se ping 192.168.200.10 — CAPWAP ke through end to end success

note.en: One config on the WLC lights up the SSID on every joined AP — the core operational win of the split-MAC architecture. Remember: WPA2 = AES/CCMP; the old WPA used TKIP.
note.hi: WLC par ek config se har joined AP par SSID chalu ho jata hai — split-MAC architecture ka yahi core operational fayda hai. Yaad rakho: WPA2 = AES/CCMP; purana WPA TKIP use karta tha.

objective.en: Populate a routing table with connected, local and loopback routes, then use longest-prefix-match logic to predict forwarding decisions.
objective.hi: Routing table ko connected, local aur loopback routes se bharo, phir longest-prefix-match logic se forwarding decisions predict karo.

tasks.en: Build the topology. Configure R1: interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown; interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.2.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown.
tasks.hi: Topology banao. R1 configure karo: interface g0/0 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown; interface g0/1 ip address 192.168.2.1 255.255.255.0, no shutdown.

tasks.en: Add a loopback (always-up test interface): interface loopback 0, ip address 10.99.99.1 255.255.255.255, end.
tasks.hi: Ek loopback add karo (hamesha up rehne wala test interface): interface loopback 0, ip address 10.99.99.1 255.255.255.255, end.

tasks.en: Run show ip route. Decode every line: C = connected network, L = local (the router's own /32 address on that network), and your loopback. Match each route to its exit interface.
tasks.hi: show ip route chalao. Har line decode karo: C = connected network, L = local (us network par router ka apna /32 address), aur tumhara loopback. Har route ko uske exit interface se match karo.

tasks.en: Answer on paper, then check against the table: which route forwards a packet to 192.168.2.77? To 10.99.99.1? To 8.8.8.8? (Answers: the C 192.168.2.0/24 route; the loopback; NO route — the packet is dropped since there is no default route.)
tasks.hi: Pehle paper par answer do, phir table se check karo: 192.168.2.77 ke liye packet kaunsa route forward karega? 10.99.99.1 ke liye? 8.8.8.8 ke liye? (Answers: C 192.168.2.0/24 route; loopback; KOI route nahi — default route nahi hai isliye packet drop ho jata hai.)

tasks.en: Prove the last answer: from PC1 ping 8.8.8.8 and watch it fail with no route on R1.
tasks.hi: Aakhri answer prove karo: PC1 se ping 8.8.8.8 karo aur dekho R1 par route na hone ki wajah se fail hota hai.

tasks.en: Longest match drill: note that L routes are /32 and always beat their parent C /24 for the router's own address — the most specific prefix always wins.
tasks.hi: Longest match drill: note karo ki L routes /32 hote hain aur router ke apne address ke liye hamesha apne parent C /24 ko beat karte hain — sabse specific prefix hamesha jeetta hai.

tasks.en: On paper write the administrative distances to memorize: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120.
tasks.hi: Paper par yaad karne wale administrative distances likho: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120.

tasks.en: Run show ip route 192.168.2.10 (a specific lookup) and read the exact matched route and exit interface.
tasks.hi: show ip route 192.168.2.10 chalao (specific lookup) aur exact matched route aur exit interface padho.

verify.en: show ip route — two C/L pairs plus the loopback entry
verify.hi: show ip route — do C/L pairs plus loopback entry

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — success through R1
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — R1 ke through success

verify.en: ping 8.8.8.8 from PC1 — fails (no default route exists)
verify.hi: PC1 se ping 8.8.8.8 — fail (koi default route nahi hai)

verify.en: AD list — written from memory and checked: 0, 1, 20, 90, 110, 120
verify.hi: AD list — yaad se likhi aur check ki: 0, 1, 20, 90, 110, 120

note.en: Route selection order: longest prefix match first; administrative distance only breaks ties between different SOURCES of the same prefix; metric breaks ties within one protocol.
note.hi: Route selection order: pehle longest prefix match; administrative distance sirf same prefix ke alag-alag SOURCES ke beech tie todta hai; metric ek protocol ke andar tie todta hai.

title.hi: Static, Default aur Floating Static Routes

objective.en: Connect two routers with primary and backup links, reach remote networks with static routes, and configure a floating static that takes over on failure.
objective.hi: Do routers ko primary aur backup links se jodo, static routes se remote networks tak pahuncho, aur ek floating static configure karo jo failure par kaam sambhal le.

tasks.en: Use two 1941 routers and add the HWIC-2T serial module to each (power off the router in the Physical tab, drag the module in, power on).
tasks.hi: Do 1941 routers use karo aur har ek mein HWIC-2T serial module add karo (Physical tab mein router power off karo, module andar drag karo, power on karo).

tasks.en: Address the primary link: R1 g0/1 = 10.0.0.1/30, R2 g0/1 = 10.0.0.2/30. Backup serial link: R1 s0/0/0 = 10.0.1.1/30, R2 s0/0/0 = 10.0.1.2/30 (add clock rate 128000 on the DCE side if prompted). LANs: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24 with PC1 = .10; R2 g0/0 = 192.168.2.1/24 with PC2 = .10.
tasks.hi: Primary link address karo: R1 g0/1 = 10.0.0.1/30, R2 g0/1 = 10.0.0.2/30. Backup serial link: R1 s0/0/0 = 10.0.1.1/30, R2 s0/0/0 = 10.0.1.2/30 (prompt aaye toh DCE side par clock rate 128000 add karo). LANs: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24 aur PC1 = .10; R2 g0/0 = 192.168.2.1/24 aur PC2 = .10.

tasks.en: On R1 add the primary static route: ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2.
tasks.hi: R1 par primary static route add karo: ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2.

tasks.en: On R2 add the return route: ip route 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.1. Test PC1 ping PC2.
tasks.hi: R2 par return route add karo: ip route 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.1. PC1 se PC2 ping test karo.

tasks.en: Add floating backups with a worse administrative distance: on R1, ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.2 90; on R2, ip route 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.1 90.
tasks.hi: Worse administrative distance ke saath floating backups add karo: R1 par ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.2 90; R2 par ip route 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.1.1 90.

tasks.en: Run show ip route on R1 — only the AD-1 primary static appears; the floating route sits hidden until it is needed.
tasks.hi: R1 par show ip route chalao — sirf AD-1 wala primary static dikhta hai; floating route tab tak chhupa rehta hai jab tak uski zaroorat na pade.

tasks.en: Fail the primary: on R1, interface g0/1, shutdown. Re-run show ip route — the floating static (AD 90) has been installed. PC1 ping PC2 still works over serial.
tasks.hi: Primary ko fail karo: R1 par interface g0/1, shutdown. show ip route dobara chalao — floating static (AD 90) install ho gaya hai. PC1 se PC2 ping abhi bhi serial par chalta hai.

tasks.en: Restore with no shutdown and confirm the AD-1 route returns to the table.
tasks.hi: no shutdown se restore karo aur confirm karo ki AD-1 route table mein wapas aa gaya.

tasks.en: Add a default route on R1 (ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.0.0.2) and observe S* in show ip route — the gateway of last resort for any destination with no better match.
tasks.hi: R1 par ek default route add karo (ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.0.0.2) aur show ip route mein S* dekho — yeh har us destination ke liye gateway of last resort hai jiska koi better match nahi.

verify.en: show ip route on R1 — S 192.168.2.0/24 via 10.0.0.2 under normal conditions
verify.hi: R1 par show ip route — normal conditions mein S 192.168.2.0/24 via 10.0.0.2

verify.en: show ip route after shutdown — the same prefix now via 10.0.1.2 (the floating route)
verify.hi: shutdown ke baad show ip route — wahi prefix ab via 10.0.1.2 (floating route)

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — works before, during and after the failover
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — failover se pehle, uske dauraan aur baad mein chalta hai

verify.en: show ip route — S* 0.0.0.0/0 listed as gateway of last resort
verify.hi: show ip route — S* 0.0.0.0/0 gateway of last resort ke roop mein listed

note.en: A floating static works because its AD (here 90) is worse than the primary's (1); IOS installs only the best AD per prefix, keeping the backup dormant until the primary vanishes.
note.hi: Floating static isliye kaam karta hai kyunki uska AD (yahan 90) primary ke (1) se worse hai; IOS har prefix ke liye sirf best AD install karta hai, aur backup ko tab tak dormant rakhta hai jab tak primary gayab na ho jaye.

objective.en: Bring up OSPFv2 between two routers, watch the neighbor reach FULL state, and inspect the DR/BDR election and interface costs.
objective.hi: Do routers ke beech OSPFv2 up karo, neighbor ko FULL state tak pahunchte dekho, aur DR/BDR election aur interface costs inspect karo.

tasks.en: Connect two 1941s G0/0-to-G0/0 (crossover). Address R1 g0/0 = 10.0.12.1/30 and R2 g0/0 = 10.0.12.2/30, both no shutdown.
tasks.hi: Do 1941s ko G0/0-to-G0/0 (crossover) se jodo. R1 g0/0 = 10.0.12.1/30 aur R2 g0/0 = 10.0.12.2/30 address karo, dono no shutdown.

tasks.en: Create loopbacks: R1 interface loopback 0 ip address 1.1.1.1 255.255.255.255; R2 loopback 0 = 2.2.2.2/32.
tasks.hi: Loopbacks banao: R1 interface loopback 0 ip address 1.1.1.1 255.255.255.255; R2 loopback 0 = 2.2.2.2/32.

tasks.en: Enable OSPF on R1: router ospf 1, router-id 1.1.1.1, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 1.1.1.1 0.0.0.0 area 0.
tasks.hi: R1 par OSPF enable karo: router ospf 1, router-id 1.1.1.1, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 1.1.1.1 0.0.0.0 area 0.

tasks.en: Enable OSPF on R2: router ospf 1, router-id 2.2.2.2, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 2.2.2.2 0.0.0.0 area 0. Watch the console print the adjacency message ending in 'LOADING to FULL'.
tasks.hi: R2 par OSPF enable karo: router ospf 1, router-id 2.2.2.2, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 2.2.2.2 0.0.0.0 area 0. Dekho console adjacency message print karta hai jo 'LOADING to FULL' par khatam hota hai.

tasks.en: Run show ip ospf neighbor on R1: one neighbor (2.2.2.2), state FULL, and a DR/BDR role — on an Ethernet (broadcast) network the two routers elect a DR and BDR; with equal priority 1, the higher router-id (2.2.2.2) becomes DR.
tasks.hi: R1 par show ip ospf neighbor chalao: ek neighbor (2.2.2.2), state FULL, aur ek DR/BDR role — Ethernet (broadcast) network par dono routers DR aur BDR elect karte hain; priority barabar 1 hone par higher router-id (2.2.2.2) DR banta hai.

tasks.en: Run show ip route ospf on R1 — the O route to 2.2.2.2/32 with metric via 10.0.12.2. Ping 2.2.2.2 to confirm.
tasks.hi: R1 par show ip route ospf chalao — 2.2.2.2/32 ka O route metric ke saath via 10.0.12.2. Confirm karne ke liye 2.2.2.2 ping karo.

tasks.en: Inspect the interface: show ip ospf interface g0/0 — find hello interval 10, dead interval 40, the network type BROADCAST, and the cost (with default reference bandwidth 100 Mbps, a GigabitEthernet port shows cost 1).
tasks.hi: Interface inspect karo: show ip ospf interface g0/0 — hello interval 10, dead interval 40, network type BROADCAST, aur cost dhoondo (default reference bandwidth 100 Mbps ke saath GigabitEthernet port cost 1 dikhata hai).

tasks.en: Change the cost and observe: interface g0/0, ip ospf cost 50, then re-check show ip ospf interface g0/0 and the metric in show ip route ospf on the OTHER router stays driven by ITS inbound costs — cost is applied outbound per interface along the path.
tasks.hi: Cost badlo aur observe karo: interface g0/0, ip ospf cost 50, phir show ip ospf interface g0/0 dobara check karo; DOOSRE router par show ip route ospf mein metric USKE apne inbound costs se hi decide hota hai — cost path ke har interface par outbound apply hoti hai.

tasks.en: Run show ip protocols and read which networks OSPF is advertising and the configured router-id.
tasks.hi: show ip protocols chalao aur padho ki OSPF kaunse networks advertise kar raha hai aur configured router-id kya hai.

verify.en: show ip ospf neighbor — state FULL/DR or FULL/BDR with neighbor ID 2.2.2.2 (from R1)
verify.hi: show ip ospf neighbor — state FULL/DR ya FULL/BDR, neighbor ID 2.2.2.2 (R1 se)

verify.en: show ip route ospf — O 2.2.2.2/32 learned via 10.0.12.2
verify.hi: show ip route ospf — O 2.2.2.2/32 via 10.0.12.2 se learned

verify.en: ping 2.2.2.2 from R1 — success
verify.hi: R1 se ping 2.2.2.2 — success

verify.en: show ip ospf interface g0/0 — hello 10, dead 40, network type BROADCAST
verify.hi: show ip ospf interface g0/0 — hello 10, dead 40, network type BROADCAST

note.en: OSPF cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth (default reference 100 Mbps, so FastEthernet and anything faster all show cost 1 unless you raise auto-cost reference-bandwidth).
note.hi: OSPF cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth (default reference 100 Mbps, isliye FastEthernet aur usse tez sab cost 1 dikhate hain jab tak tum auto-cost reference-bandwidth nahi badhate).

objective.en: Configure single-area OSPFv2 across a three-router triangle with a LAN on each router, using router-ids, wildcard-correct network statements and passive interfaces.
objective.hi: Teen routers ke triangle par single-area OSPFv2 configure karo, har router par ek LAN ke saath, router-ids, sahi wildcard wale network statements aur passive interfaces use karke.

topology: R1 (G0/1) — (G0/1) R2; R2 (G0/2) — (G0/2) R3; R3 (G0/1) — (G0/2) R1; each router G0/0 — switch — one PC

tasks.en: Use three 2911 routers (they have three Gig ports). Address the links: R1-R2 = 10.0.12.0/30 (.1 and .2), R2-R3 = 10.0.23.0/30 (.2 is R2... use R2 = 10.0.23.1, R3 = 10.0.23.2), R1-R3 = 10.0.13.0/30 (R1 = .1, R3 = .2). All interfaces no shutdown.
tasks.hi: Teen 2911 routers use karo (inme teen Gig ports hote hain). Links address karo: R1-R2 = 10.0.12.0/30 (.1 aur .2), R2-R3 = 10.0.23.0/30 (.2 is R2... R2 = 10.0.23.1, R3 = 10.0.23.2 use karo), R1-R3 = 10.0.13.0/30 (R1 = .1, R3 = .2). Saare interfaces no shutdown.

tasks.en: Address the LANs: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24 with PC1 = .10, R2 g0/0 = 192.168.2.1/24 with PC2 = .10, R3 g0/0 = 192.168.3.1/24 with PC3 = .10 (PCs point at their local router as gateway).
tasks.hi: LANs address karo: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24 aur PC1 = .10, R2 g0/0 = 192.168.2.1/24 aur PC2 = .10, R3 g0/0 = 192.168.3.1/24 aur PC3 = .10 (PCs apne local router ko gateway banate hain).

tasks.en: R1 OSPF: router ospf 1, router-id 1.1.1.1, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.13.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, passive-interface g0/0.
tasks.hi: R1 OSPF: router ospf 1, router-id 1.1.1.1, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.13.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, passive-interface g0/0.

tasks.en: R2 OSPF: router ospf 1, router-id 2.2.2.2, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.23.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, passive-interface g0/0.
tasks.hi: R2 OSPF: router ospf 1, router-id 2.2.2.2, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.23.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, passive-interface g0/0.

tasks.en: R3 OSPF: router ospf 1, router-id 3.3.3.3, network 10.0.13.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.23.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 192.168.3.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, passive-interface g0/0.
tasks.hi: R3 OSPF: router ospf 1, router-id 3.3.3.3, network 10.0.13.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.23.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 192.168.3.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, passive-interface g0/0.

tasks.en: Verify adjacencies: show ip ospf neighbor on each router should list TWO neighbors in FULL state (with DR/BDR roles per link).
tasks.hi: Adjacencies verify karo: har router par show ip ospf neighbor mein FULL state wale DO neighbors hone chahiye (har link par DR/BDR roles ke saath).

tasks.en: Verify routes: show ip route ospf on R1 shows O routes to 192.168.2.0/24, 192.168.3.0/24 and the far /30 (10.0.23.0/30) — note the equal-path situation to remote LANs is not equal here (direct link cost 1 beats two hops), so each LAN is reached via its direct link.
tasks.hi: Routes verify karo: R1 par show ip route ospf mein 192.168.2.0/24, 192.168.3.0/24 aur door wale /30 (10.0.23.0/30) ke O routes dikhte hain — note karo ki remote LANs tak ka path yahan equal nahi hai (direct link cost 1 do hops ko beat karta hai), isliye har LAN apne direct link se reach hota hai.

tasks.en: End-to-end test: PC1 ping PC2 and PC3. Then trace the failover: shutdown R1 g0/1 (the R1-R2 link) and confirm PC1 can still ping PC2 — OSPF reroutes via R3. Bring the link back up.
tasks.hi: End-to-end test: PC1 se PC2 aur PC3 ko ping karo. Phir failover trace karo: R1 g0/1 (R1-R2 link) shutdown karo aur confirm karo ki PC1 abhi bhi PC2 ko ping kar sakta hai — OSPF R3 ke through reroute karta hai. Link wapas up karo.

tasks.en: Confirm passive interfaces: show ip ospf interface g0/0 or show ip protocols — the LAN interface is advertised into OSPF but sends no hellos toward the PCs.
tasks.hi: Passive interfaces confirm karo: show ip ospf interface g0/0 ya show ip protocols — LAN interface OSPF mein advertise hota hai lekin PCs ki taraf koi hellos nahi bhejta.

verify.en: show ip ospf neighbor on all three routers — two FULL neighbors each
verify.hi: teeno routers par show ip ospf neighbor — har ek par do FULL neighbors

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC3 — success; still successful with the R1-R2 link shut (rerouted)
verify.hi: PC1 se PC3 ping — success; R1-R2 link shut hone par bhi success (rerouted)

verify.en: show ip protocols — passive interface g0/0 listed, router-id correct
verify.hi: show ip protocols — passive interface g0/0 listed, router-id sahi

note.en: The wildcard mask is the inverse of the subnet mask (/30 = 0.0.0.3, /24 = 0.0.0.255). passive-interface on LAN ports is both a security and an efficiency best practice.
note.hi: Wildcard mask subnet mask ka ulta hota hai (/30 = 0.0.0.3, /24 = 0.0.0.255). LAN ports par passive-interface security aur efficiency dono ke liye best practice hai.

objective.en: Deliberately break an OSPF adjacency four different ways and repair each one using the neighbor-formation mismatch checklist.
objective.hi: OSPF adjacency ko jaan-boojh kar chaar alag tareekon se todo aur har ek ko neighbor-formation mismatch checklist se repair karo.

tasks.en: Rebuild lab-26's working two-router OSPF (or reopen the saved file). Confirm show ip ospf neighbor shows FULL before you begin. Save the config.
tasks.hi: lab-26 ka working two-router OSPF dobara banao (ya saved file kholo). Shuru karne se pehle confirm karo ki show ip ospf neighbor FULL dikhata hai. Config save karo.

tasks.en: Write the mismatch checklist you will test: same subnet/mask, same area, hello/dead timers match, interface not passive, no authentication mismatch, MTU match — and remember router-ids must be UNIQUE.
tasks.hi: Jo mismatch checklist test karoge use likho: same subnet/mask, same area, hello/dead timers match, interface passive nahi, authentication mismatch nahi, MTU match — aur yaad rakho router-ids UNIQUE hone chahiye.

tasks.en: Break 1 — wrong area: on R2, router ospf 1, no network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 1. The adjacency drops (console message). Diagnose with show ip ospf interface g0/0 on both sides (area 0 vs area 1). Fix by restoring area 0 and confirm FULL returns.
tasks.hi: Break 1 — galat area: R2 par router ospf 1, no network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0, network 10.0.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 1. Adjacency drop ho jati hai (console message). Dono sides par show ip ospf interface g0/0 se diagnose karo (area 0 vs area 1). area 0 restore karke fix karo aur confirm karo ki FULL wapas aata hai.

tasks.en: Break 2 — hello timer mismatch: on R2, interface g0/0, ip ospf hello-interval 5. The neighbor drops after the dead timer expires. Compare show ip ospf interface g0/0 on both routers (hello 10 vs 5 — dead interval auto-follows to 20). Fix with no ip ospf hello-interval and watch FULL return.
tasks.hi: Break 2 — hello timer mismatch: R2 par interface g0/0, ip ospf hello-interval 5. Dead timer expire hone ke baad neighbor drop ho jata hai. Dono routers par show ip ospf interface g0/0 compare karo (hello 10 vs 5 — dead interval apne aap 20 ho jata hai). no ip ospf hello-interval se fix karo aur FULL wapas aate dekho.

tasks.en: Break 3 — passive interface: on R1, router ospf 1, passive-interface g0/0. Hellos stop leaving R1; the neighbor dies. Spot it in show ip protocols under passive interfaces. Fix with no passive-interface g0/0.
tasks.hi: Break 3 — passive interface: R1 par router ospf 1, passive-interface g0/0. R1 se hellos jaana band ho jaate hain; neighbor mar jata hai. show ip protocols mein passive interfaces ke neeche ise pakdo. no passive-interface g0/0 se fix karo.

tasks.en: Break 4 — subnet mismatch: on R2, interface g0/0, ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.0 (wrong mask). Neighbors on a broadcast network must agree on the subnet; the adjacency fails. Fix with ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252.
tasks.hi: Break 4 — subnet mismatch: R2 par interface g0/0, ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.0 (galat mask). Broadcast network par neighbors ko subnet par agree karna padta hai; adjacency fail hoti hai. ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252 se fix karo.

tasks.en: After each fix, wait for the console 'FULL' message and re-run show ip ospf neighbor before injecting the next fault — one variable at a time.
tasks.hi: Har fix ke baad console ke 'FULL' message ka wait karo aur agla fault daalne se pehle show ip ospf neighbor dobara chalao — ek time par ek hi variable.

tasks.en: Close out: write the checklist from memory on a card for the week 8 super labs.
tasks.hi: Close out: week 8 super labs ke liye checklist ko yaad se ek card par likho.

verify.en: show ip ospf neighbor — returns to FULL after every one of the four fixes
verify.hi: show ip ospf neighbor — chaaron fixes mein se har ek ke baad FULL par wapas aata hai

verify.en: show ip ospf interface g0/0 — used to expose the area and timer mismatches
verify.hi: show ip ospf interface g0/0 — area aur timer mismatches pakadne ke liye use kiya

verify.en: show ip protocols — used to expose the passive interface
verify.hi: show ip protocols — passive interface pakadne ke liye use kiya

verify.en: Your checklist card — area, subnet, timers, passive, authentication, MTU, unique router-id
verify.hi: Tumhara checklist card — area, subnet, timers, passive, authentication, MTU, unique router-id

note.en: Timers and area must MATCH; router-ids must DIFFER. Duplicate router-ids are a classic silent failure — the routers log a message and refuse to form or flap the adjacency.
note.hi: Timers aur area MATCH hone chahiye; router-ids ALAG hone chahiye. Duplicate router-ids ek classic silent failure hai — routers ek message log karte hain aur adjacency banane se mana kar dete hain ya use flap karte hain.

objective.en: Give a LAN a resilient default gateway with HSRP, control the active router with priority and preemption, and prove failover with a live ping.
objective.hi: HSRP se LAN ko ek resilient default gateway do, priority aur preemption se active router control karo, aur live ping se failover prove karo.

tasks.en: Build the topology: one 2960, two 1941s, one PC. Both routers connect to the SAME switch and LAN.
tasks.hi: Topology banao: ek 2960, do 1941s, ek PC. Dono routers SAME switch aur LAN se connect hote hain.

tasks.en: Address the real interfaces: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, R2 g0/0 = 192.168.1.2/24, both no shutdown.
tasks.hi: Real interfaces address karo: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, R2 g0/0 = 192.168.1.2/24, dono no shutdown.

tasks.en: Configure HSRP on R1 (intended active): interface g0/0, standby version 2, standby 1 ip 192.168.1.254, standby 1 priority 110, standby 1 preempt.
tasks.hi: R1 (jise active banana hai) par HSRP configure karo: interface g0/0, standby version 2, standby 1 ip 192.168.1.254, standby 1 priority 110, standby 1 preempt.

tasks.en: Configure HSRP on R2 (standby): interface g0/0, standby version 2, standby 1 ip 192.168.1.254. (Default priority is 100 — lower than R1's 110.)
tasks.hi: R2 (standby) par HSRP configure karo: interface g0/0, standby version 2, standby 1 ip 192.168.1.254. (Default priority 100 hai — R1 ke 110 se kam.)

tasks.en: Point PC1 at the VIRTUAL gateway: 192.168.1.10/24, gateway 192.168.1.254.
tasks.hi: PC1 ko VIRTUAL gateway par point karo: 192.168.1.10/24, gateway 192.168.1.254.

tasks.en: Run show standby brief on both routers: R1 shows Active, R2 shows Standby, virtual IP 192.168.1.254. Note the virtual MAC in show standby (HSRPv2 uses 0000.0c9f.fxxx where xxx is the group).
tasks.hi: Dono routers par show standby brief chalao: R1 Active dikhata hai, R2 Standby, virtual IP 192.168.1.254. show standby mein virtual MAC note karo (HSRPv2 0000.0c9f.fxxx use karta hai jahan xxx group hai).

tasks.en: From PC1 start a long test: ping 192.168.1.254 -n 50 (Desktop > Command Prompt).
tasks.hi: PC1 se ek lamba test start karo: ping 192.168.1.254 -n 50 (Desktop > Command Prompt).

tasks.en: While it runs, kill the active router: on R1, interface g0/0, shutdown. A few pings drop, then replies resume — R2 has become Active (watch its console print the state change). Confirm with show standby brief on R2.
tasks.hi: Jab yeh chal raha ho, active router ko maar do: R1 par interface g0/0, shutdown. Kuch pings drop hote hain, phir replies wapas aane lagte hain — R2 Active ban gaya hai (uske console par state change print hote dekho). R2 par show standby brief se confirm karo.

tasks.en: Recover R1 with no shutdown: because R1 has preempt configured and higher priority, it reclaims Active. Verify with show standby brief on both routers.
tasks.hi: R1 ko no shutdown se recover karo: kyunki R1 par preempt configured hai aur uski priority zyada hai, woh Active wapas le leta hai. Dono routers par show standby brief se verify karo.

verify.en: show standby brief on R1 — Group 1, Priority 110, State Active, Virtual IP 192.168.1.254 (before failover)
verify.hi: R1 par show standby brief — Group 1, Priority 110, State Active, Virtual IP 192.168.1.254 (failover se pehle)

verify.en: show standby brief on R2 during R1's outage — State Active
verify.hi: R1 ke outage ke dauraan R2 par show standby brief — State Active

verify.en: ping 192.168.1.254 -n 50 from PC1 — loses only a handful of packets across the failover
verify.hi: PC1 se ping 192.168.1.254 -n 50 — failover ke dauraan sirf kuch hi packets lose hote hain

verify.en: show standby brief after no shutdown — R1 Active again, proving preemption
verify.hi: no shutdown ke baad show standby brief — R1 phir se Active, jo preemption prove karta hai

note.en: Without 'standby 1 preempt', a recovered R1 would sit in Standby forever even with higher priority. HSRP is Cisco-proprietary; VRRP is the open equivalent and GLBP adds load balancing — know all three names for the exam.
note.hi: 'standby 1 preempt' ke bina recovered R1 zyada priority hone ke bawajood hamesha Standby mein hi baitha rehta. HSRP Cisco-proprietary hai; VRRP iska open equivalent hai aur GLBP load balancing add karta hai — exam ke liye teeno naam jaano.

title.en: Static NAT & PAT Overload to a Simulated ISP
title.hi: Simulated ISP tak Static NAT aur PAT Overload

objective.en: Publish an internal server with static NAT and give a whole LAN internet access with PAT overload, verified from both sides of a simulated ISP.
objective.hi: Ek internal server ko static NAT se publish karo aur poore LAN ko PAT overload se internet access do, simulated ISP ki dono sides se verify karke.

tasks.en: Build the topology with two 1941s (R1 and ISP). Inside LAN: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, PC1 = .10, Web-SRV (Server-PT, HTTP on) = .100, gateways 192.168.1.1. Outside link: R1 g0/1 = 203.0.113.1/29, ISP g0/0 = 203.0.113.2/29. ISP LAN: ISP g0/1 = 198.51.100.1/24, Net-Host = 198.51.100.50 gateway 198.51.100.1.
tasks.hi: Do 1941s (R1 aur ISP) ke saath topology banao. Inside LAN: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, PC1 = .10, Web-SRV (Server-PT, HTTP on) = .100, gateways 192.168.1.1. Outside link: R1 g0/1 = 203.0.113.1/29, ISP g0/0 = 203.0.113.2/29. ISP LAN: ISP g0/1 = 198.51.100.1/24, Net-Host = 198.51.100.50 gateway 198.51.100.1.

tasks.en: Give R1 a default route to the ISP: ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.2. Do NOT give the ISP any route to 192.168.1.0/24 — the internet never routes RFC 1918 space; NAT must hide it.
tasks.hi: R1 ko ISP ki taraf default route do: ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 203.0.113.2. ISP ko 192.168.1.0/24 ka koi route MAT do — internet kabhi RFC 1918 space route nahi karta; NAT ko ise chhupana hi padega.

tasks.en: Mark the NAT domains on R1: interface g0/0, ip nat inside; interface g0/1, ip nat outside.
tasks.hi: R1 par NAT domains mark karo: interface g0/0, ip nat inside; interface g0/1, ip nat outside.

tasks.en: Prove the problem first: from PC1 ping 198.51.100.50 — it fails (the ISP has no return route to 192.168.1.0/24).
tasks.hi: Pehle problem prove karo: PC1 se ping 198.51.100.50 — fail hota hai (ISP ke paas 192.168.1.0/24 ka return route nahi hai).

tasks.en: Configure PAT overload for the LAN: access-list 1 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255, then ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload.
tasks.hi: LAN ke liye PAT overload configure karo: access-list 1 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255, phir ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload.

tasks.en: Re-test: PC1 ping 198.51.100.50 now succeeds. Immediately run show ip nat translations on R1 and read the entry: inside local 192.168.1.10 mapped to inside global 203.0.113.1 with unique port numbers.
tasks.hi: Dobara test karo: PC1 se ping 198.51.100.50 ab succeed hota hai. Turant R1 par show ip nat translations chalao aur entry padho: inside local 192.168.1.10 inside global 203.0.113.1 par mapped hai, unique port numbers ke saath.

tasks.en: Publish the web server with static NAT: ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.100 203.0.113.5.
tasks.hi: Web server ko static NAT se publish karo: ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.100 203.0.113.5.

tasks.en: From Net-Host open the web browser to http://203.0.113.5 — the inside server's page loads even though its real address is private.
tasks.hi: Net-Host se web browser mein http://203.0.113.5 kholo — inside server ka page load hota hai jabki uska real address private hai.

tasks.en: Run show ip nat statistics and identify: total translations, the inside and outside interfaces, and hits climbing as you repeat the tests.
tasks.hi: show ip nat statistics chalao aur pehchano: total translations, inside aur outside interfaces, aur tests repeat karne par badhte hue hits.

verify.en: ping 198.51.100.50 from PC1 — fails before NAT, succeeds after the overload rule
verify.hi: PC1 se ping 198.51.100.50 — NAT se pehle fail, overload rule ke baad success

verify.en: show ip nat translations — PAT entries with ports for PC1, plus the static 192.168.1.100 to 203.0.113.5 mapping
verify.hi: show ip nat translations — PC1 ki ports wali PAT entries, plus static 192.168.1.100 se 203.0.113.5 mapping

verify.en: http://203.0.113.5 from Net-Host — inside web page loads via static NAT
verify.hi: Net-Host se http://203.0.113.5 — static NAT se inside web page load hota hai

verify.en: show ip nat statistics — inside/outside interfaces listed correctly
verify.hi: show ip nat statistics — inside/outside interfaces sahi listed

note.en: Vocabulary the exam drills: inside local (private, as seen inside), inside global (public, as seen outside), outside global (the far-end public address). PAT multiplexes thousands of flows on one public IP using source ports.
note.hi: Exam jo vocabulary baar-baar poochta hai: inside local (private, andar se jaisa dikhta hai), inside global (public, bahar se jaisa dikhta hai), outside global (door wale end ka public address). PAT source ports use karke ek public IP par hazaron flows multiplex karta hai.

title.en: DHCP with Relay plus Enterprise DNS
title.hi: Relay ke saath DHCP plus Enterprise DNS

objective.en: Serve DHCP to a remote LAN through an ip helper-address relay, resolve names with an internal DNS server, and configure a router-hosted IOS pool.
objective.hi: ip helper-address relay ke through ek remote LAN ko DHCP serve karo, internal DNS server se names resolve karo, aur ek router-hosted IOS pool configure karo.

topology: PC1, PC2 — SW1 — (G0/0) R1 (G0/1) — SW2 — Server1 (192.168.2.100: DHCP, DNS, HTTP) and PC3

tasks.en: Build the topology. R1: g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, g0/1 = 192.168.2.1/24, both no shutdown. Server1 static: 192.168.2.100/24 gateway 192.168.2.1.
tasks.hi: Topology banao. R1: g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, g0/1 = 192.168.2.1/24, dono no shutdown. Server1 static: 192.168.2.100/24 gateway 192.168.2.1.

tasks.en: On Server1 enable DHCP with a pool FOR THE REMOTE LAN: default gateway 192.168.1.1, DNS server 192.168.2.100, start IP 192.168.1.50, mask 255.255.255.0.
tasks.hi: Server1 par REMOTE LAN KE LIYE pool ke saath DHCP enable karo: default gateway 192.168.1.1, DNS server 192.168.2.100, start IP 192.168.1.50, mask 255.255.255.0.

tasks.en: On Server1 enable DNS with an A record: www.ccna.lab = 192.168.2.100. Leave HTTP on.
tasks.hi: Server1 par DNS enable karo ek A record ke saath: www.ccna.lab = 192.168.2.100. HTTP on rehne do.

tasks.en: Set PC1 to DHCP and watch it FAIL (APIPA 169.254.x.x address) — its broadcast DHCPDISCOVER cannot cross R1 to reach the server.
tasks.hi: PC1 ko DHCP par set karo aur dekho woh FAIL hota hai (APIPA 169.254.x.x address) — uska broadcast DHCPDISCOVER R1 ko cross karke server tak nahi pahunch sakta.

tasks.en: Add the relay on the CLIENT-facing interface: R1, interface g0/0, ip helper-address 192.168.2.100. The router now converts LAN 1's DHCP broadcasts into unicasts to the server.
tasks.hi: CLIENT-facing interface par relay add karo: R1, interface g0/0, ip helper-address 192.168.2.100. Ab router LAN 1 ke DHCP broadcasts ko server ke liye unicasts mein convert karta hai.

tasks.en: Renew PC1 and PC2 (toggle to Static and back to DHCP, or use ipconfig /renew in the command prompt) — both should receive 192.168.1.50+ addresses with the right gateway and DNS.
tasks.hi: PC1 aur PC2 renew karo (Static par toggle karke wapas DHCP par, ya command prompt mein ipconfig /renew) — dono ko sahi gateway aur DNS ke saath 192.168.1.50+ addresses milne chahiye.

tasks.en: From PC1 browse to http://www.ccna.lab — DNS resolves the name to 192.168.2.100 and the page loads. Also try nslookup www.ccna.lab in PC1's command prompt.
tasks.hi: PC1 se http://www.ccna.lab browse karo — DNS naam ko 192.168.2.100 mein resolve karta hai aur page load hota hai. PC1 ke command prompt mein nslookup www.ccna.lab bhi try karo.

tasks.en: Now build an IOS-hosted pool for LAN 2's PC3 on R1: ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.2.1 192.168.2.100, then ip dhcp pool LAN2, network 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0, default-router 192.168.2.1, dns-server 192.168.2.100.
tasks.hi: Ab R1 par LAN 2 ke PC3 ke liye IOS-hosted pool banao: ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.2.1 192.168.2.100, phir ip dhcp pool LAN2, network 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0, default-router 192.168.2.1, dns-server 192.168.2.100.

tasks.en: Set PC3 to DHCP, confirm it gets 192.168.2.101 or higher, then run show ip dhcp binding on R1 to see the lease.
tasks.hi: PC3 ko DHCP par set karo, confirm karo ki use 192.168.2.101 ya usse upar milta hai, phir lease dekhne ke liye R1 par show ip dhcp binding chalao.

verify.en: PC1 IP Configuration — 192.168.1.5x with gateway 192.168.1.1 and DNS 192.168.2.100 (via relay)
verify.hi: PC1 IP Configuration — 192.168.1.5x, gateway 192.168.1.1 aur DNS 192.168.2.100 (relay ke through)

verify.en: http://www.ccna.lab from PC1 — page loads; nslookup returns 192.168.2.100
verify.hi: PC1 se http://www.ccna.lab — page load hota hai; nslookup 192.168.2.100 return karta hai

verify.en: show ip dhcp binding on R1 — PC3's lease from the IOS pool
verify.hi: R1 par show ip dhcp binding — IOS pool se PC3 ki lease

verify.en: show ip dhcp pool LAN2 (or show running-config) — pool parameters as configured
verify.hi: show ip dhcp pool LAN2 (ya show running-config) — pool parameters jaise configure kiye

note.en: If PC3 ever grabs a lease from Server1 instead of the IOS pool, temporarily switch the server's DHCP service off while testing PC3 — two DHCP servers answering one segment race each other, itself a real-world lesson.
note.hi: Agar PC3 kabhi IOS pool ki jagah Server1 se lease le le, toh PC3 test karte waqt server ki DHCP service thodi der ke liye off kar do — ek segment par do DHCP servers answer karein toh unme race hoti hai, aur yeh khud ek real-world lesson hai.

title.hi: NTP, Syslog aur SNMP par ek Nazar

objective.en: Synchronize router time to an NTP server, ship timestamped syslog messages to a central collector, and read a device MIB with SNMP.
objective.hi: Router ka time NTP server se synchronize karo, timestamped syslog messages central collector ko bhejo, aur SNMP se device MIB padho.

topology: PC1 (Fa0) — (F0/1) SW1 (F0/24) — (G0/0) R1; Server1 (NTP, Syslog services, Fa0) — (F0/2) SW1

tasks.en: On Server1 > Services turn NTP On (note the service page also lets you set authentication — leave it off for now). Turn the Syslog service On as well.
tasks.hi: Server1 > Services par NTP On karo (note karo ki service page par authentication bhi set kar sakte ho — abhi ise off rehne do). Syslog service bhi On karo.

tasks.en: Check R1's clock first: show clock — note it is wrong (Packet Tracer defaults to an old date).
tasks.hi: Pehle R1 ki clock check karo: show clock — note karo ki yeh galat hai (Packet Tracer default mein purani date rakhta hai).

tasks.en: Point R1 at the time source: configure terminal, ntp server 192.168.1.100.
tasks.hi: R1 ko time source par point karo: configure terminal, ntp server 192.168.1.100.

tasks.en: Wait a minute of simulation time, then run show ntp status (look for 'Clock is synchronized') and show clock — the time now matches the server.
tasks.hi: Simulation time ka ek minute wait karo, phir show ntp status chalao ('Clock is synchronized' dhoondo) aur show clock — time ab server se match karta hai.

tasks.en: Make log messages useful: service timestamps log datetime msec, then send them off-box with logging 192.168.1.100.
tasks.hi: Log messages ko useful banao: service timestamps log datetime msec, phir logging 192.168.1.100 se unhe box ke bahar bhejo.

tasks.en: Generate log events: interface g0/0, shutdown, wait a moment, no shutdown, end. Each transition produces LINK-UPDOWN and LINEPROTO-UPDOWN messages.
tasks.hi: Log events generate karo: interface g0/0, shutdown, thoda ruko, no shutdown, end. Har transition LINK-UPDOWN aur LINEPROTO-UPDOWN messages banata hai.

tasks.en: Open Server1 > Services > Syslog and read the collected messages with their timestamps — central logging in action.
tasks.hi: Server1 > Services > Syslog kholo aur collected messages unke timestamps ke saath padho — yeh hai central logging action mein.

tasks.en: SNMP peek: on R1 configure snmp-server community ccnaRO ro, then on PC1 open Desktop > MIB Browser, set target 192.168.1.1 with community ccnaRO, and walk to .iso.org.dod.internet.mgmt.mib-2.system.sysName — a GET returns the hostname R1.
tasks.hi: SNMP peek: R1 par snmp-server community ccnaRO ro configure karo, phir PC1 par Desktop > MIB Browser kholo, target 192.168.1.1 community ccnaRO ke saath set karo, aur .iso.org.dod.internet.mgmt.mib-2.system.sysName tak walk karo — GET hostname R1 return karta hai.

verify.en: show ntp status — Clock is synchronized, stratum shown, reference 192.168.1.100
verify.hi: show ntp status — Clock is synchronized, stratum dikhta hai, reference 192.168.1.100

verify.en: show clock — current (synchronized) time instead of the stale default
verify.hi: show clock — purane default ki jagah current (synchronized) time

verify.en: Server1 Syslog service — interface up/down messages with msec timestamps listed
verify.hi: Server1 Syslog service — msec timestamps ke saath interface up/down messages listed

verify.en: MIB Browser GET of sysName — returns R1 using the ccnaRO community
verify.hi: sysName ka MIB Browser GET — ccnaRO community use karke R1 return karta hai

note.en: NTP stratum counts distance from the reference clock (stratum 1 = directly attached). RO vs RW SNMP communities matter for the exam — never leave 'public'/'private' defaults in production. Syslog severities 0-7: remember 'Every Awesome Cisco Engineer Will Need Ice-cream Daily' (emergency to debugging).
note.hi: NTP stratum reference clock se doori ginta hai (stratum 1 = directly attached). Exam ke liye RO vs RW SNMP communities matter karti hain — production mein 'public'/'private' defaults kabhi mat chhodo. Syslog severities 0-7: yaad rakho 'Every Awesome Cisco Engineer Will Need Ice-cream Daily' (emergency se debugging tak).

title.hi: SSH Management aur TFTP Config Backup

objective.en: Replace Telnet with SSHv2 using local credentials, then back up the router configuration to a TFTP server and confirm the file arrived.
objective.hi: Local credentials ke saath Telnet ki jagah SSHv2 lagao, phir router configuration ka TFTP server par backup lo aur confirm karo ki file pahunch gayi.

topology: PC1 (Fa0) — (F0/1) SW1 (F0/24) — (G0/0) R1; Server1 (TFTP, Fa0) — (F0/2) SW1

tasks.en: Build the topology. R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24; PC1 = 192.168.1.10/24 gateway .1; Server1 = 192.168.1.100/24 (its TFTP service is on by default).
tasks.hi: Topology banao. R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24; PC1 = 192.168.1.10/24 gateway .1; Server1 = 192.168.1.100/24 (iski TFTP service default se on hai).

tasks.en: SSH prerequisites on R1: hostname R1 (already set), then ip domain-name ccna.lab — the RSA key is generated from hostname plus domain.
tasks.hi: R1 par SSH prerequisites: hostname R1 (pehle se set), phir ip domain-name ccna.lab — RSA key hostname plus domain se generate hoti hai.

tasks.en: Create the login: username admin privilege 15 secret Admin123!
tasks.hi: Login banao: username admin privilege 15 secret Admin123!

tasks.en: Generate the key pair: crypto key generate rsa — when prompted 'How many bits in the modulus', enter 1024 (or higher).
tasks.hi: Key pair generate karo: crypto key generate rsa — jab 'How many bits in the modulus' poocha jaye, 1024 (ya zyada) daalo.

tasks.en: Force version 2: ip ssh version 2.
tasks.hi: Version 2 force karo: ip ssh version 2.

tasks.en: Lock the vty lines to SSH with local login: line vty 0 4, transport input ssh, login local, exec-timeout 5 0, end. Also set enable secret Class123! if not already present.
tasks.hi: vty lines ko local login ke saath SSH par lock karo: line vty 0 4, transport input ssh, login local, exec-timeout 5 0, end. Agar pehle se nahi hai toh enable secret Class123! bhi set karo.

tasks.en: Test from PC1's command prompt: ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 — accept, enter Admin123!, and land at the R1 prompt. Type exit.
tasks.hi: PC1 ke command prompt se test karo: ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 — accept karo, Admin123! daalo, aur R1 prompt par pahuncho. exit type karo.

tasks.en: Negative test: from PC1 run telnet 192.168.1.1 — the connection is refused because the vty lines accept only SSH.
tasks.hi: Negative test: PC1 se telnet 192.168.1.1 chalao — connection refuse hota hai kyunki vty lines sirf SSH accept karti hain.

tasks.en: Back up the config over the network: on R1 run copy running-config tftp: — remote host 192.168.1.100, destination filename R1-confg. Then open Server1 > Services > TFTP and find R1-confg in the file list.
tasks.hi: Network par config ka backup lo: R1 par copy running-config tftp: chalao — remote host 192.168.1.100, destination filename R1-confg. Phir Server1 > Services > TFTP kholo aur file list mein R1-confg dhoondo.

tasks.en: Bonus restore drill (read-only): note the reverse command you would use — copy tftp: running-config — and why merging vs replacing matters.
tasks.hi: Bonus restore drill (read-only): ulta command note karo jo tum use karoge — copy tftp: running-config — aur yeh bhi ki merging vs replacing kyun matter karta hai.

verify.en: ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 from PC1 — successful login to the R1 prompt
verify.hi: PC1 se ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 — R1 prompt par successful login

verify.en: telnet 192.168.1.1 from PC1 — connection refused
verify.hi: PC1 se telnet 192.168.1.1 — connection refused

verify.en: show ip ssh on R1 — SSH Enabled, version 2.0
verify.hi: R1 par show ip ssh — SSH Enabled, version 2.0

verify.en: Server1 TFTP file list — R1-confg present after the copy
verify.hi: Server1 TFTP file list — copy ke baad R1-confg present

note.en: The exam checklist for 'SSH will not enable': hostname set, domain-name set, RSA keys generated (1024-bit minimum for SSHv2), and vty lines set to login local with transport input ssh.
note.hi: 'SSH enable nahi ho raha' ke liye exam checklist: hostname set, domain-name set, RSA keys generated (SSHv2 ke liye minimum 1024-bit), aur vty lines par login local aur transport input ssh set.

title.en: Services Super Lab: NAT + DHCP + NTP from Memory
title.hi: Services Super Lab: NAT + DHCP + NTP Yaad se

objective.en: Rebuild the week's core services — DHCP, PAT overload and NTP — in one topology from memory, with notes closed and a 45-minute timebox.
objective.hi: Hafte ki core services — DHCP, PAT overload aur NTP — ko ek topology mein yaad se dobara banao, notes band karke aur 45-minute timebox ke saath.

topology: PC1, PC2 — SW1 — (G0/0) R1 (G0/1) — (G0/0) ISP (G0/1) — SW2 — Server1 (203.0.113.100: HTTP and NTP)

tasks.en: Set a 45-minute timer. Close all notes and lessons — only the requirements below are allowed. Build the topology: R1-ISP link = 198.51.100.0/30 (R1 = .1, ISP = .2), ISP LAN = 203.0.113.0/24 (ISP g0/1 = .1, Server1 = .100), inside LAN = 192.168.1.0/24 on R1 g0/0.
tasks.hi: 45-minute timer set karo. Saare notes aur lessons band kar do — sirf neeche di gayi requirements allowed hain. Topology banao: R1-ISP link = 198.51.100.0/30 (R1 = .1, ISP = .2), ISP LAN = 203.0.113.0/24 (ISP g0/1 = .1, Server1 = .100), inside LAN = 192.168.1.0/24 R1 g0/0 par.

tasks.en: Requirement 1 — DHCP: PC1 and PC2 must receive addresses from an IOS pool on R1 (network 192.168.1.0/24, gateway 192.168.1.1, DNS 203.0.113.100, with .1 through .49 excluded).
tasks.hi: Requirement 1 — DHCP: PC1 aur PC2 ko R1 par ek IOS pool se addresses milne chahiye (network 192.168.1.0/24, gateway 192.168.1.1, DNS 203.0.113.100, aur .1 se .49 tak excluded).

tasks.en: Requirement 2 — routing: R1 has a default route to the ISP; the ISP router must have NO route to 192.168.1.0/24.
tasks.hi: Requirement 2 — routing: R1 ke paas ISP ki taraf default route ho; ISP router ke paas 192.168.1.0/24 ka KOI route nahi hona chahiye.

tasks.en: Requirement 3 — PAT: every inside host must reach 203.0.113.100 through an interface overload translation on R1.
tasks.hi: Requirement 3 — PAT: har inside host ko R1 par interface overload translation ke through 203.0.113.100 tak pahunchna chahiye.

tasks.en: Requirement 4 — NTP: R1 must synchronize its clock to Server1 (enable the server's NTP service).
tasks.hi: Requirement 4 — NTP: R1 ko apni clock Server1 se synchronize karni chahiye (server ki NTP service enable karo).

tasks.en: Requirement 5 — proof: from PC1, ping 203.0.113.100 and load http://203.0.113.100 in the browser; on R1 capture show ip nat translations while the browser session is active.
tasks.hi: Requirement 5 — proof: PC1 se 203.0.113.100 ping karo aur browser mein http://203.0.113.100 load karo; jab browser session active ho tab R1 par show ip nat translations capture karo.

tasks.en: When the timer ends, reopen your notes and score yourself: one point per requirement fully working (5 max).
tasks.hi: Timer khatam hone par notes dobara kholo aur khud ko score karo: har poori tarah kaam karne wali requirement ka ek point (max 5).

tasks.en: For every requirement you missed or had to look up, write the exact commands you forgot into your error log — those commands are your week 6 flashcard additions.
tasks.hi: Har woh requirement jo miss hui ya jiske liye dekhna pada, uske bhoole hue exact commands apne error log mein likho — yahi commands tumhare week 6 flashcards mein add honge.

tasks.en: Save the file as services-superlab.pkt; week 8's lab-42 will ask you to beat this time.
tasks.hi: File ko services-superlab.pkt naam se save karo; week 8 ka lab-42 tumse yeh time beat karne ko kahega.

verify.en: PC1 and PC2 IP Configuration — DHCP addresses at 192.168.1.50 or above
verify.hi: PC1 aur PC2 IP Configuration — 192.168.1.50 ya usse upar ke DHCP addresses

verify.en: show ip nat translations on R1 — active PAT entries during the web test
verify.hi: R1 par show ip nat translations — web test ke dauraan active PAT entries

verify.en: show ntp status on R1 — Clock is synchronized to 203.0.113.100
verify.hi: R1 par show ntp status — Clock is synchronized to 203.0.113.100

verify.en: http://203.0.113.100 from PC1 — page loads end to end
verify.hi: PC1 se http://203.0.113.100 — page end to end load hota hai

verify.en: Self-score sheet — 5/5 requirements or an error-log entry for each gap
verify.hi: Self-score sheet — 5/5 requirements ya har gap ke liye ek error-log entry

note.en: From-memory practice is the highest-value study activity this week: the exam's lab-sim items give you requirements, not commands.
note.hi: Is hafte yaad se practice karna sabse zyada value wali study activity hai: exam ke lab-sim items tumhe requirements dete hain, commands nahi.

objective.en: Harden a router's management plane: encrypted secrets, console and vty protection, a legal banner, and SSH-only remote access with a local user database.
objective.hi: Router ka management plane harden karo: encrypted secrets, console aur vty protection, legal banner, aur local user database ke saath sirf SSH wala remote access.

tasks.en: Protect privileged EXEC: enable secret Class123! (secret = MD5-hashed; never use the legacy 'enable password').
tasks.hi: Privileged EXEC protect karo: enable secret Class123! (secret = MD5-hashed; legacy 'enable password' kabhi use mat karo).

tasks.en: Protect the console: line console 0, password Cisco123, login, exec-timeout 5 0, exit.
tasks.hi: Console protect karo: line console 0, password Cisco123, login, exec-timeout 5 0, exit.

tasks.en: Hide plaintext passwords from casual reads: service password-encryption (type-7 obfuscation for line passwords).
tasks.hi: Casual nazar se plaintext passwords chhupao: service password-encryption (line passwords ke liye type-7 obfuscation).

tasks.en: Add a legal banner: banner motd #Authorized access only. Activity is monitored.# — note the # delimiters and that a banner must never say 'welcome'.
tasks.hi: Legal banner add karo: banner motd #Authorized access only. Activity is monitored.# — # delimiters note karo, aur yeh bhi ki banner mein kabhi 'welcome' nahi likhna chahiye.

tasks.en: Create the local admin: username admin privilege 15 secret Admin123!
tasks.hi: Local admin banao: username admin privilege 15 secret Admin123!

tasks.en: Secure remote access (SSH prep): ip domain-name ccna.lab, crypto key generate rsa (1024 bits), ip ssh version 2, then line vty 0 4, login local, transport input ssh, exec-timeout 5 0, end.
tasks.hi: Remote access secure karo (SSH prep): ip domain-name ccna.lab, crypto key generate rsa (1024 bits), ip ssh version 2, phir line vty 0 4, login local, transport input ssh, exec-timeout 5 0, end.

tasks.en: Test each control: exit the console session and reconnect (banner shows, console password required); from PC1 ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 (works) and telnet 192.168.1.1 (refused).
tasks.hi: Har control test karo: console session se exit karke reconnect karo (banner dikhta hai, console password maanga jata hai); PC1 se ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 (chalta hai) aur telnet 192.168.1.1 (refused).

tasks.en: Inspect show running-config: the enable secret shows a type 5 hash, the console password shows type 7, the username shows a secret hash — identify each.
tasks.hi: show running-config inspect karo: enable secret type 5 hash dikhata hai, console password type 7, username ek secret hash — har ek pehchano.

tasks.en: Paper AAA exercise: write three lines contrasting local AAA (what you just built) with server-based AAA — TACACS+ (Cisco, TCP 49, encrypts full payload, command authorization) vs RADIUS (open standard, UDP 1812/1813, encrypts only the password, strong accounting).
tasks.hi: Paper AAA exercise: teen lines likho jo local AAA (jo tumne abhi banaya) ko server-based AAA se contrast karein — TACACS+ (Cisco, TCP 49, poora payload encrypt karta hai, command authorization) vs RADIUS (open standard, UDP 1812/1813, sirf password encrypt karta hai, strong accounting).

verify.en: Console reconnect — MOTD banner displays, then the console password is demanded
verify.hi: Console reconnect — MOTD banner dikhta hai, phir console password maanga jata hai

verify.en: ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 from PC1 — login succeeds; telnet is refused
verify.hi: PC1 se ssh -l admin 192.168.1.1 — login succeed hota hai; telnet refused hota hai

verify.en: show running-config — enable secret hashed (type 5) and line passwords obfuscated (type 7)
verify.hi: show running-config — enable secret hashed (type 5) aur line passwords obfuscated (type 7)

verify.en: AAA notes — TACACS+ TCP 49 vs RADIUS UDP 1812/1813 recorded correctly
verify.hi: AAA notes — TACACS+ TCP 49 vs RADIUS UDP 1812/1813 sahi likhe hue

note.en: Password type ranking for the exam: type 0 (plaintext) worst, type 7 trivially reversible, type 5 (MD5) acceptable, types 8/9 (PBKDF2/scrypt) best on modern IOS. 'secret' always beats 'password'.
note.hi: Exam ke liye password type ranking: type 0 (plaintext) sabse bura, type 7 aasaani se reverse ho jata hai, type 5 (MD5) acceptable, types 8/9 (PBKDF2/scrypt) modern IOS par best. 'secret' hamesha 'password' ko beat karta hai.

objective.en: Filter traffic with a numbered standard ACL placed near the destination and a named extended ACL placed near the source, verifying hit counts as you test.
objective.hi: Destination ke paas lagaye numbered standard ACL aur source ke paas lagaye named extended ACL se traffic filter karo, aur test karte hue hit counts verify karo.

tasks.en: Build the topology. R1: g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, g0/1 = 192.168.2.1/24. Hosts as in the topology diagram, gateways at their local router interface. Server1 has HTTP on. Confirm PC1 can ping PC3 and load http://192.168.2.100 before filtering.
tasks.hi: Topology banao. R1: g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24, g0/1 = 192.168.2.1/24. Hosts topology diagram ke hisaab se, gateways unke local router interface par. Server1 par HTTP on hai. Filtering se pehle confirm karo ki PC1, PC3 ko ping kar sakta hai aur http://192.168.2.100 load kar sakta hai.

tasks.en: Standard ACL (filters on SOURCE only, so place near the DESTINATION): access-list 10 deny host 192.168.1.11, then access-list 10 permit any.
tasks.hi: Standard ACL (sirf SOURCE par filter karta hai, isliye DESTINATION ke paas lagao): access-list 10 deny host 192.168.1.11, phir access-list 10 permit any.

tasks.en: Apply it outbound where the protected LAN exits the router: interface g0/1, ip access-group 10 out, end.
tasks.hi: Ise outbound wahan apply karo jahan protected LAN router se nikalta hai: interface g0/1, ip access-group 10 out, end.

tasks.en: Test: PC2 (the .11 host) can no longer ping PC3 or reach the server; PC1 still can. Run show access-lists and watch the deny counter increment as PC2 retries.
tasks.hi: Test: PC2 (.11 host) ab PC3 ko ping nahi kar sakta ya server tak nahi pahunch sakta; PC1 abhi bhi kar sakta hai. show access-lists chalao aur dekho PC2 ke retry karne par deny counter badhta hai.

tasks.en: Remove the standard ACL before the next exercise: interface g0/1, no ip access-group 10 out.
tasks.hi: Agli exercise se pehle standard ACL hatao: interface g0/1, no ip access-group 10 out.

tasks.en: Named extended ACL (matches protocol/ports, so place near the SOURCE): ip access-list extended BLOCK-WEB, deny tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.2.100 eq 80, permit ip any any, exit.
tasks.hi: Named extended ACL (protocol/ports match karta hai, isliye SOURCE ke paas lagao): ip access-list extended BLOCK-WEB, deny tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.2.100 eq 80, permit ip any any, exit.

tasks.en: Apply it inbound on the source LAN's interface: interface g0/0, ip access-group BLOCK-WEB in, end.
tasks.hi: Ise source LAN ke interface par inbound apply karo: interface g0/0, ip access-group BLOCK-WEB in, end.

tasks.en: Test the precision: from PC1 the browser to http://192.168.2.100 now FAILS, but ping 192.168.2.100 still WORKS — only TCP port 80 is filtered.
tasks.hi: Precision test karo: PC1 se browser mein http://192.168.2.100 ab FAIL hota hai, lekin ping 192.168.2.100 abhi bhi CHALTA hai — sirf TCP port 80 filter hua hai.

tasks.en: Run show access-lists — read the per-line match counters, and note the invisible implicit deny any at the end of every ACL (why the permit ip any any line was mandatory).
tasks.hi: show access-lists chalao — har line ke match counters padho, aur har ACL ke end mein invisible implicit deny any note karo (isi wajah se permit ip any any line zaroori thi).

tasks.en: Paper drill: write the wildcard masks for /24, /26 and /30 (0.0.0.255, 0.0.0.63, 0.0.0.3) and state the placement rule: standard near destination, extended near source.
tasks.hi: Paper drill: /24, /26 aur /30 ke wildcard masks likho (0.0.0.255, 0.0.0.63, 0.0.0.3) aur placement rule batao: standard destination ke paas, extended source ke paas.

verify.en: show access-lists — ACL 10 deny line shows match counters from PC2's blocked pings
verify.hi: show access-lists — ACL 10 deny line PC2 ke blocked pings se match counters dikhati hai

verify.en: PC2 to PC3 — blocked while ACL 10 applied; PC1 unaffected
verify.hi: PC2 se PC3 — ACL 10 apply rehne tak blocked; PC1 par koi asar nahi

verify.en: After BLOCK-WEB — http://192.168.2.100 fails from PC1 but ping 192.168.2.100 succeeds
verify.hi: BLOCK-WEB ke baad — PC1 se http://192.168.2.100 fail hota hai lekin ping 192.168.2.100 succeed hota hai

verify.en: show running-config interface g0/0 — ip access-group BLOCK-WEB in present
verify.hi: show running-config interface g0/0 — ip access-group BLOCK-WEB in present

note.en: One ACL per interface, per direction, per protocol. Order matters: IOS processes top-down and stops at the first match — put specific lines before general ones.
note.hi: Har interface, har direction, har protocol par ek ACL. Order matter karta hai: IOS top-down process karta hai aur first match par ruk jata hai — specific lines ko general lines se pehle rakho.

title.hi: Port Security, DHCP Snooping aur DAI

objective.en: Defend the access layer three ways: sticky port security against unknown MACs, DHCP snooping against rogue servers, and Dynamic ARP Inspection against ARP spoofing.
objective.hi: Access layer ko teen tareekon se defend karo: unknown MACs ke against sticky port security, rogue servers ke against DHCP snooping, aur ARP spoofing ke against Dynamic ARP Inspection.

topology: DHCP-SRV (Fa0) — (F0/24) SW1; PC1 — (F0/1) SW1; PC2 — (F0/2) SW1; Rogue-PC (spare, initially unplugged)

tasks.en: Build the topology: one 2960, a Server-PT running DHCP (pool for 192.168.1.0/24, gateway 192.168.1.1, start IP 192.168.1.50, server static at 192.168.1.100), two PCs set to DHCP, and a spare Rogue-PC left unplugged.
tasks.hi: Topology banao: ek 2960, DHCP chala raha ek Server-PT (192.168.1.0/24 ka pool, gateway 192.168.1.1, start IP 192.168.1.50, server static 192.168.1.100 par), DHCP par set do PCs, aur ek spare Rogue-PC jo unplugged rahe.

tasks.en: Confirm PC1 and PC2 receive DHCP leases.
tasks.hi: Confirm karo ki PC1 aur PC2 ko DHCP leases mil rahi hain.

tasks.en: Port security on the PC ports: interface range f0/1 - 2, switchport mode access, switchport port-security, switchport port-security maximum 1, switchport port-security mac-address sticky, switchport port-security violation shutdown, end. (Port security requires a static access port — 'dynamic' mode ports reject it.)
tasks.hi: PC ports par port security: interface range f0/1 - 2, switchport mode access, switchport port-security, switchport port-security maximum 1, switchport port-security mac-address sticky, switchport port-security violation shutdown, end. (Port security ke liye static access port chahiye — 'dynamic' mode wale ports ise reject kar dete hain.)

tasks.en: Generate traffic (ping from PC1 to PC2) so the switch learns and sticks the MACs, then check show port-security interface f0/1 and show running-config (the sticky MAC now appears as a config line).
tasks.hi: Traffic generate karo (PC1 se PC2 ko ping) taaki switch MACs seekh kar unhe stick kar le, phir show port-security interface f0/1 aur show running-config check karo (sticky MAC ab ek config line ke roop mein dikhta hai).

tasks.en: Violation test: unplug PC1 from F0/1 and plug Rogue-PC into F0/1. Its first frame trips the violation — the port goes err-disabled (red light). Confirm with show port-security interface f0/1 (status secure-shutdown, violation count 1).
tasks.hi: Violation test: PC1 ko F0/1 se unplug karo aur Rogue-PC ko F0/1 mein plug karo. Uska pehla frame hi violation trip kar deta hai — port err-disabled ho jata hai (red light). show port-security interface f0/1 se confirm karo (status secure-shutdown, violation count 1).

tasks.en: Recover: reconnect the real PC1, then interface f0/1, shutdown, no shutdown.
tasks.hi: Recover karo: asli PC1 dobara connect karo, phir interface f0/1, shutdown, no shutdown.

tasks.en: DHCP snooping: globally ip dhcp snooping and ip dhcp snooping vlan 1; then trust ONLY the server uplink: interface f0/24, ip dhcp snooping trust. Untrusted ports (the PC ports) can now send DHCP client messages but any DHCPOFFER from them is dropped — a rogue DHCP server on F0/1 or F0/2 is neutralized.
tasks.hi: DHCP snooping: globally ip dhcp snooping aur ip dhcp snooping vlan 1; phir SIRF server uplink ko trust karo: interface f0/24, ip dhcp snooping trust. Untrusted ports (PC ports) ab DHCP client messages bhej sakte hain lekin unse aane wala koi bhi DHCPOFFER drop hota hai — F0/1 ya F0/2 par rogue DHCP server neutralize ho jata hai.

tasks.en: Renew PC1 and PC2 leases, then run show ip dhcp snooping binding — the table maps each client MAC to its IP, port and VLAN. This table is DAI's source of truth.
tasks.hi: PC1 aur PC2 ki leases renew karo, phir show ip dhcp snooping binding chalao — table har client MAC ko uske IP, port aur VLAN se map karti hai. Yahi table DAI ka source of truth hai.

tasks.en: Dynamic ARP Inspection: globally ip arp inspection vlan 1, and trust the server uplink: interface f0/24, ip arp inspection trust. Untrusted ports now have their ARP packets checked against the snooping bindings — spoofed ARP replies (wrong IP-to-MAC) are dropped.
tasks.hi: Dynamic ARP Inspection: globally ip arp inspection vlan 1, aur server uplink ko trust karo: interface f0/24, ip arp inspection trust. Ab untrusted ports ke ARP packets snooping bindings se check hote hain — spoofed ARP replies (galat IP-to-MAC) drop ho jaate hain.

tasks.en: Verify the whole stack: show ip dhcp snooping (mode and trusted ports), show ip arp inspection vlan 1, and confirm PC1 and PC2 still ping each other normally (legitimate traffic is untouched).
tasks.hi: Poora stack verify karo: show ip dhcp snooping (mode aur trusted ports), show ip arp inspection vlan 1, aur confirm karo ki PC1 aur PC2 abhi bhi normally ek doosre ko ping karte hain (legitimate traffic par koi asar nahi).

verify.en: show port-security interface f0/1 — secure-shutdown with violation count 1 during the rogue test; secure-up after recovery
verify.hi: show port-security interface f0/1 — rogue test ke dauraan secure-shutdown, violation count 1; recovery ke baad secure-up

verify.en: show ip dhcp snooping — snooping enabled on VLAN 1, F0/24 trusted
verify.hi: show ip dhcp snooping — VLAN 1 par snooping enabled, F0/24 trusted

verify.en: show ip dhcp snooping binding — entries for PC1 and PC2 with correct MAC/IP/port
verify.hi: show ip dhcp snooping binding — PC1 aur PC2 ki entries sahi MAC/IP/port ke saath

verify.en: show ip arp inspection vlan 1 — DAI active; PC1 to PC2 ping still succeeds
verify.hi: show ip arp inspection vlan 1 — DAI active; PC1 se PC2 ping abhi bhi succeed

note.en: The three features chain together: snooping builds the binding table, DAI consumes it, and port security caps who can even talk. Trust points always face the legitimate infrastructure, never the users.
note.hi: Teeno features ek chain mein kaam karte hain: snooping binding table banata hai, DAI use consume karta hai, aur port security limit karta hai ki baat kaun kar sakta hai. Trust points hamesha legitimate infrastructure ki taraf hote hain, users ki taraf kabhi nahi.

title.en: Site-to-Site IPsec VPN & Wireless Security Matrix
title.hi: Site-to-Site IPsec VPN aur Wireless Security Matrix

objective.en: Tunnel two private LANs across an untrusted core router with an IPsec site-to-site VPN, then summarize WPA generations in a comparison matrix.
objective.hi: IPsec site-to-site VPN se do private LANs ko ek untrusted core router ke paar tunnel karo, phir WPA generations ko ek comparison matrix mein summarize karo.

tasks.en: Build with three 2911 routers (R1, INET, R3). Links: R1-INET = 10.1.12.0/30 (R1 = .1), INET-R3 = 10.1.23.0/30 (R3 = .2). LANs: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24 with PC1 = .10; R3 g0/0 = 192.168.2.1/24 with PC2 = .10. Default routes: R1 ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.1.12.2; R3 ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.1.23.1. INET gets NO routes to either LAN — it is the untrusted internet.
tasks.hi: Teen 2911 routers (R1, INET, R3) se banao. Links: R1-INET = 10.1.12.0/30 (R1 = .1), INET-R3 = 10.1.23.0/30 (R3 = .2). LANs: R1 g0/0 = 192.168.1.1/24 aur PC1 = .10; R3 g0/0 = 192.168.2.1/24 aur PC2 = .10. Default routes: R1 ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.1.12.2; R3 ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.1.23.1. INET ko kisi bhi LAN ka KOI route nahi milta — yeh untrusted internet hai.

tasks.en: Prove the problem: PC1 ping PC2 fails (INET drops packets for unknown private LANs).
tasks.hi: Problem prove karo: PC1 se PC2 ping fail hota hai (INET unknown private LANs ke packets drop karta hai).

tasks.en: Enable the crypto feature set on R1 and R3: license boot module c2900 technology-package securityk9, accept the EULA, copy running-config startup-config, then reload each router.
tasks.hi: R1 aur R3 par crypto feature set enable karo: license boot module c2900 technology-package securityk9, EULA accept karo, copy running-config startup-config, phir har router reload karo.

tasks.en: Phase 1 (IKE) policy on BOTH R1 and R3: crypto isakmp policy 10, encryption aes 256, authentication pre-share, group 5, exit. Pre-shared keys: on R1 crypto isakmp key VPNpass123 address 10.1.23.2; on R3 crypto isakmp key VPNpass123 address 10.1.12.1.
tasks.hi: R1 aur R3 DONO par Phase 1 (IKE) policy: crypto isakmp policy 10, encryption aes 256, authentication pre-share, group 5, exit. Pre-shared keys: R1 par crypto isakmp key VPNpass123 address 10.1.23.2; R3 par crypto isakmp key VPNpass123 address 10.1.12.1.

tasks.en: Phase 2 transform set on both: crypto ipsec transform-set VPN-SET esp-aes esp-sha-hmac.
tasks.hi: Dono par Phase 2 transform set: crypto ipsec transform-set VPN-SET esp-aes esp-sha-hmac.

tasks.en: Define interesting traffic: on R1 access-list 110 permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255; on R3 the mirror image access-list 110 permit ip 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255.
tasks.hi: Interesting traffic define karo: R1 par access-list 110 permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255; R3 par mirror image access-list 110 permit ip 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255.

tasks.en: Crypto map on R1: crypto map VPN-MAP 10 ipsec-isakmp, set peer 10.1.23.2, set transform-set VPN-SET, match address 110, exit, then apply with interface g0/1, crypto map VPN-MAP. Mirror on R3 (peer 10.1.12.1) applied to its g0/1.
tasks.hi: R1 par crypto map: crypto map VPN-MAP 10 ipsec-isakmp, set peer 10.1.23.2, set transform-set VPN-SET, match address 110, exit, phir interface g0/1, crypto map VPN-MAP se apply karo. R3 par mirror karo (peer 10.1.12.1) aur uske g0/1 par apply karo.
