tasks.en: Trigger the tunnel: PC1 ping PC2 — the first packet or two may drop while IKE negotiates, then replies flow. INET now only sees ESP packets between the two public /30 addresses.
tasks.hi: Tunnel trigger karo: PC1 se PC2 ping — IKE negotiate hote waqt pehla ek-do packet drop ho sakta hai, phir replies aane lagte hain. Ab INET ko do public /30 addresses ke beech sirf ESP packets dikhte hain.

tasks.en: Verify the SAs: show crypto isakmp sa (state QM_IDLE) and show crypto ipsec sa (pkts encaps and pkts decaps climbing with each ping).
tasks.hi: SAs verify karo: show crypto isakmp sa (state QM_IDLE) aur show crypto ipsec sa (har ping ke saath pkts encaps aur pkts decaps badhte hain).

tasks.en: Paper matrix: three columns WPA / WPA2 / WPA3 — cipher (TKIP / AES-CCMP / AES-GCMP), key exchange (PSK 4-way / PSK 4-way / SAE), and one extra (WPA3 adds forward secrecy and management frame protection). Add a final row for Enterprise mode: 802.1X with a RADIUS server instead of a passphrase.
tasks.hi: Paper matrix: teen columns WPA / WPA2 / WPA3 — cipher (TKIP / AES-CCMP / AES-GCMP), key exchange (PSK 4-way / PSK 4-way / SAE), aur ek extra (WPA3 forward secrecy aur management frame protection add karta hai). Aakhir mein Enterprise mode ki ek row add karo: passphrase ki jagah RADIUS server ke saath 802.1X.

verify.en: ping PC1 to PC2 — fails before the VPN, succeeds after (first packets may time out during IKE)
verify.hi: PC1 se PC2 ping — VPN se pehle fail, baad mein success (IKE ke dauraan pehle packets time out ho sakte hain)

verify.en: show crypto isakmp sa — peer entry in state QM_IDLE
verify.hi: show crypto isakmp sa — peer entry state QM_IDLE mein

verify.en: show crypto ipsec sa — pkts encaps/decaps counters increasing with traffic
verify.hi: show crypto ipsec sa — traffic ke saath pkts encaps/decaps counters badh rahe hain

verify.en: WPA matrix — TKIP/CCMP/GCMP and PSK/PSK/SAE rows completed correctly
verify.hi: WPA matrix — TKIP/CCMP/GCMP aur PSK/PSK/SAE rows sahi bhari hui

note.en: IPsec vocabulary: IKE/ISAKMP builds the control channel (phase 1), the IPsec SA carries data (phase 2), ESP encrypts, AH only authenticates. Site-to-site protects networks; remote-access VPNs protect single clients.
note.hi: IPsec vocabulary: IKE/ISAKMP control channel banata hai (phase 1), IPsec SA data carry karta hai (phase 2), ESP encrypt karta hai, AH sirf authenticate karta hai. Site-to-site networks ko protect karta hai; remote-access VPNs single clients ko protect karte hain.

title.en: REST API Anatomy & a Live Sandbox Call
title.hi: REST API Anatomy aur Live Sandbox Call

objective.en: Dissect REST mechanics — CRUD verbs, URI anatomy, status codes and token auth — then exercise a real controller API in Cisco's free DevNet sandbox.
objective.hi: REST mechanics ko kholkar samjho — CRUD verbs, URI anatomy, status codes aur token auth — phir Cisco ke free DevNet sandbox mein ek real controller API chala kar dekho.

topology: None in Packet Tracer — a real web browser plus the free Cisco DevNet Always-On sandbox (paper worksheet for the offline parts)

tasks.en: Write the CRUD-to-HTTP table from memory, then check it: Create = POST, Read = GET, Update = PUT (full replace) or PATCH (partial), Delete = DELETE.
tasks.hi: CRUD-to-HTTP table yaad se likho, phir check karo: Create = POST, Read = GET, Update = PUT (full replace) ya PATCH (partial), Delete = DELETE.

tasks.en: Dissect this URI on paper, labeling each part: https://dnac.example.com/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device?managementIpAddress=10.10.22.74 — scheme, host, path (the resource), and query parameter (the filter).
tasks.hi: Is URI ko paper par dissect karo, har part label karke: https://dnac.example.com/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device?managementIpAddress=10.10.22.74 — scheme, host, path (resource), aur query parameter (filter).

tasks.en: Classify these status codes into buckets: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Server Error. Rule: 2xx success, 4xx your fault, 5xx their fault.
tasks.hi: In status codes ko buckets mein classify karo: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Server Error. Rule: 2xx success, 4xx tumhari galti, 5xx unki galti.

tasks.en: Write two sentences on token authentication: the client first POSTs credentials to an auth endpoint, receives a token, and sends it on every later request in a header such as X-Auth-Token — so credentials travel once, not per call.
tasks.hi: Token authentication par do sentences likho: client pehle credentials ko ek auth endpoint par POST karta hai, ek token leta hai, aur baad ki har request mein use X-Auth-Token jaise header mein bhejta hai — yaani credentials ek baar travel karte hain, har call par nahi.

tasks.en: Live portion (real browser, free account): go to developer.cisco.com/site/sandbox and open the Catalyst Center (DNA Center) Always-On sandbox page; note its base URL and the published read-only credentials.
tasks.hi: Live hissa (real browser, free account): developer.cisco.com/site/sandbox par jao aur Catalyst Center (DNA Center) Always-On sandbox page kholo; uska base URL aur published read-only credentials note karo.

tasks.en: Open the sandbox's interactive API documentation (or the Catalyst Center GUI's Developer Toolkit) and execute the authentication POST from the docs page — copy the token string it returns.
tasks.hi: Sandbox ka interactive API documentation (ya Catalyst Center GUI ka Developer Toolkit) kholo aur docs page se authentication POST execute karo — jo token string return ho use copy karo.

tasks.en: Still in the interactive docs, run GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device using that token and read the JSON response: find the device list array and, for one device, the hostname, managementIpAddress and softwareVersion-style fields (names vary slightly by version).
tasks.hi: Interactive docs mein hi us token ke saath GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device chalao aur JSON response padho: device list array dhoondo aur ek device ke liye hostname, managementIpAddress aur softwareVersion jaise fields dhoondo (version ke hisaab se names thode alag ho sakte hain).

tasks.en: Note which REST characteristics you just used: stateless (the token accompanied every call), client-server, uniform interface, and data returned as JSON.
tasks.hi: Note karo ki tumne abhi kaunsi REST characteristics use ki: stateless (token har call ke saath gaya), client-server, uniform interface, aur data JSON mein return hua.

tasks.en: If you are offline today, complete the paper parts and mark the sandbox call as homework — do not skip it entirely; touching a real API once removes most of the exam's mystery.
tasks.hi: Agar aaj tum offline ho, toh paper wale parts poore karo aur sandbox call ko homework mark karo — ise poori tarah skip mat karo; ek baar real API chhoo lene se exam ka zyaadatar mystery khatam ho jata hai.

verify.en: CRUD table — POST/GET/PUT-PATCH/DELETE with PATCH identified as partial update
verify.hi: CRUD table — POST/GET/PUT-PATCH/DELETE, aur PATCH ko partial update identify kiya hua

verify.en: URI dissection — scheme, host, path and query labeled correctly
verify.hi: URI dissection — scheme, host, path aur query sahi labeled

verify.en: Status buckets — 2xx success, 4xx client error, 5xx server error with 401 vs 403 distinguished
verify.hi: Status buckets — 2xx success, 4xx client error, 5xx server error, aur 401 vs 403 ka fark clear

verify.en: Sandbox call — auth POST returned a token and the device GET returned JSON you could read
verify.hi: Sandbox call — auth POST ne token return kiya aur device GET ne JSON return kiya jo tum padh sake

note.en: REST is an architectural style, not a protocol: stateless, cacheable, uniform interface over HTTP. Northbound APIs (controller to apps) are REST; southbound (controller to devices) uses NETCONF/RESTCONF/SSH.
note.hi: REST ek architectural style hai, protocol nahi: HTTP par stateless, cacheable, uniform interface. Northbound APIs (controller se apps) REST hote hain; southbound (controller se devices) NETCONF/RESTCONF/SSH use karte hain.

objective.en: Parse JSON by hand with zero tooling, author valid JSON yourself, and build a comparison sheet for Ansible versus Terraform plus AI/ML network roles.
objective.hi: Bina kisi tooling ke JSON haath se parse karo, khud valid JSON likho, aur Ansible vs Terraform plus AI/ML network roles ki comparison sheet banao.

topology: None — paper worksheet (optionally type your JSON into any text editor to eyeball balance of braces)

tasks.en:
Copy this JSON onto paper exactly, then answer the questions below it:
{ "device": { "hostname": "SW1", "uptime": 45210, "mgmt": { "ip": "10.1.1.5", "vlan": 10 }, "interfaces": [ "Gig1/0/1", "Gig1/0/2" ], "poe": false } }
tasks.hi:
Is JSON ko paper par bilkul waisa hi copy karo, phir neeche diye questions ke answers do:
{ "device": { "hostname": "SW1", "uptime": 45210, "mgmt": { "ip": "10.1.1.5", "vlan": 10 }, "interfaces": [ "Gig1/0/1", "Gig1/0/2" ], "poe": false } }

tasks.en: Question set A — types: what is the JSON type of the value of uptime, of poe, of interfaces, and of mgmt? (number, boolean, array, object). Write the answers before checking verify.
tasks.hi: Question set A — types: uptime ki value ka JSON type kya hai, poe ka, interfaces ka, aur mgmt ka? (number, boolean, array, object). Verify check karne se pehle answers likh lo.

tasks.en: Question set B — access paths: what value lives at device.mgmt.vlan? How many elements are in device.interfaces? Is the 10 in mgmt.vlan a string or a number, and how can you tell? (No quotes = number.)
tasks.hi: Question set B — access paths: device.mgmt.vlan par kaunsi value hai? device.interfaces mein kitne elements hain? mgmt.vlan wala 10 string hai ya number, aur tum kaise bata sakte ho? (Quotes nahi = number.)

tasks.en: Author your own JSON describing an interface with exactly these keys: name (string), ip (string), enabled (boolean), allowedVlans (array of 3 numbers). Check your own work for the four classic errors: single quotes, unquoted keys, trailing comma after the last item, missing brace/bracket.
tasks.hi: Ek interface describe karne wala apna JSON likho jisme theek yeh keys hon: name (string), ip (string), enabled (boolean), allowedVlans (3 numbers ka array). Apne kaam ko chaar classic errors ke liye check karo: single quotes, unquoted keys, last item ke baad trailing comma, missing brace/bracket.

tasks.en: Write the Ansible vs Terraform table, 5 rows: language (YAML playbooks vs HCL), model (procedural-leaning vs declarative state), agent (agentless over SSH vs agentless via provider APIs), state file (none vs terraform.tfstate), primary sweet spot (config management and orchestration vs infrastructure provisioning).
tasks.hi: Ansible vs Terraform table likho, 5 rows: language (YAML playbooks vs HCL), model (procedural-leaning vs declarative state), agent (SSH par agentless vs provider APIs se agentless), state file (koi nahi vs terraform.tfstate), primary sweet spot (config management aur orchestration vs infrastructure provisioning).

tasks.en: Add a one-line note on push vs pull models: Ansible pushes over SSH when you run a playbook; pull-model tools (like Chef/Puppet agents) fetch config from a server on a schedule.
tasks.hi: Push vs pull models par ek line ka note add karo: jab tum playbook chalate ho tab Ansible SSH par push karta hai; pull-model tools (jaise Chef/Puppet agents) schedule par server se config fetch karte hain.

tasks.en: AI/ML in networking (v1.1): write one line each for — predictive analytics (forecast failures from telemetry), anomaly detection (baseline deviations flag attacks or faults), generative AI assistants (natural-language config/query help), and why ML needs the large telemetry streams modern controllers collect.
tasks.hi: Networking mein AI/ML (v1.1): har ek ke liye ek line likho — predictive analytics (telemetry se failures ka forecast), anomaly detection (baseline se deviations attacks ya faults flag karte hain), generative AI assistants (natural-language mein config/query help), aur ML ko modern controllers ke collect kiye bade telemetry streams kyun chahiye.

tasks.en: Self-test closure: without looking, write valid JSON for a two-VLAN object and have tomorrow-you check it against the four classic errors list.
tasks.hi: Self-test closure: bina dekhe ek two-VLAN object ka valid JSON likho aur kal wale tum use chaar classic errors ki list se check karo.

verify.en: Set A answers — number, boolean, array, object
verify.hi: Set A answers — number, boolean, array, object

verify.en: Set B answers — 10 (a number, because it is unquoted); 2 elements in interfaces
verify.hi: Set B answers — 10 (number, kyunki yeh unquoted hai); interfaces mein 2 elements

verify.en: Your authored JSON — double quotes on every key and string, no trailing commas, balanced braces/brackets
verify.hi: Tumhara likha JSON — har key aur string par double quotes, koi trailing commas nahi, braces/brackets balanced

verify.en: Ansible vs Terraform table — YAML vs HCL and agentless-SSH vs state-file rows correct
verify.hi: Ansible vs Terraform table — YAML vs HCL aur agentless-SSH vs state-file rows sahi

note.en: The exam shows JSON snippets and asks what is valid or what a value's type is. Remember: JSON allows string, number, boolean, null, object, array — no comments, no single quotes, no trailing commas.
note.hi: Exam JSON snippets dikhata hai aur poochta hai ki kya valid hai ya kisi value ka type kya hai. Yaad rakho: JSON string, number, boolean, null, object, array allow karta hai — comments nahi, single quotes nahi, trailing commas nahi.

title.en: Super Lab 1: Switching + Routing from Memory
title.hi: Super Lab 1: Switching + Routing Yaad se

objective.en: Rebuild the course's core switching and routing stack — VLANs, trunking, EtherChannel, router-on-a-stick and OSPF — from a bare requirements list, notes closed, in 60 minutes.
objective.hi: Course ka core switching aur routing stack — VLANs, trunking, EtherChannel, router-on-a-stick aur OSPF — sirf ek requirements list se, notes band karke, 60 minutes mein dobara banao.

topology: PC1 (VLAN 10) and PC2 (VLAN 20) — SW1; SW1 (F0/23, F0/24) — (F0/23, F0/24) SW2 (LACP Po1 trunk); PC3 (VLAN 10) — SW2; SW1 (G0/1) — (G0/0) R1 (G0/1) — (G0/1) R2 (G0/0) — SW3 — PC4

tasks.en: Set a 60-minute timer. Notes closed — only this requirements list. Place two 2960s (SW1, SW2), a third 2960 (SW3), two 1941s (R1, R2) and four PCs, cabled per the topology.
tasks.hi: 60-minute timer set karo. Notes band — sirf yeh requirements list. Do 2960s (SW1, SW2), ek teesra 2960 (SW3), do 1941s (R1, R2) aur chaar PCs rakho, topology ke hisaab se cabled.

tasks.en: Requirement 1 — VLANs: create VLAN 10 (Sales) and VLAN 20 (HR) on SW1 and SW2. Access ports: PC1 in 10 and PC2 in 20 on SW1; PC3 in 10 on SW2. Subnets: VLAN 10 = 192.168.10.0/24, VLAN 20 = 192.168.20.0/24 (gateways .1, hosts .11+).
tasks.hi: Requirement 1 — VLANs: SW1 aur SW2 par VLAN 10 (Sales) aur VLAN 20 (HR) banao. Access ports: SW1 par PC1 VLAN 10 mein aur PC2 VLAN 20 mein; SW2 par PC3 VLAN 10 mein. Subnets: VLAN 10 = 192.168.10.0/24, VLAN 20 = 192.168.20.0/24 (gateways .1, hosts .11+).

tasks.en: Requirement 2 — EtherChannel: bundle SW1-SW2 F0/23-24 as Po1 using LACP (active/active), configured as an 802.1Q trunk allowing VLANs 10 and 20.
tasks.hi: Requirement 2 — EtherChannel: SW1-SW2 F0/23-24 ko LACP (active/active) se Po1 ke roop mein bundle karo, aur use VLANs 10 aur 20 allow karne wale 802.1Q trunk ki tarah configure karo.

tasks.en: Requirement 3 — router-on-a-stick: SW1 G0/1 trunks to R1 G0/0; R1 subinterfaces g0/0.10 = 192.168.10.1/24 (dot1q 10) and g0/0.20 = 192.168.20.1/24 (dot1q 20).
tasks.hi: Requirement 3 — router-on-a-stick: SW1 G0/1 R1 G0/0 tak trunk karta hai; R1 subinterfaces g0/0.10 = 192.168.10.1/24 (dot1q 10) aur g0/0.20 = 192.168.20.1/24 (dot1q 20).

tasks.en: Requirement 5 — OSPF: single-area OSPF (process 1, area 0) on R1 and R2 advertising every network, router-ids 1.1.1.1 and 2.2.2.2, passive toward all LAN/subinterface segments (not the WAN).
tasks.hi: Requirement 5 — OSPF: R1 aur R2 par single-area OSPF (process 1, area 0) jo har network advertise kare, router-ids 1.1.1.1 aur 2.2.2.2, aur saare LAN/subinterface segments ki taraf passive (WAN ki taraf nahi).

tasks.en: Requirement 6 — proof: PC1 pings PC3 (VLAN 10 across the trunk), PC1 pings PC2 (routed between VLANs), and PC1 pings PC4 (OSPF across the WAN).
tasks.hi: Requirement 6 — proof: PC1 PC3 ko ping kare (trunk ke paar VLAN 10), PC1 PC2 ko ping kare (VLANs ke beech routed), aur PC1 PC4 ko ping kare (WAN ke paar OSPF).

tasks.en: When the timer stops, grade yourself with the standard outputs: show vlan brief, show etherchannel summary, show interfaces trunk, show ip ospf neighbor, show ip route ospf.
tasks.hi: Timer rukne par standard outputs se khud ko grade karo: show vlan brief, show etherchannel summary, show interfaces trunk, show ip ospf neighbor, show ip route ospf.

tasks.en: Log every command you had to think about for more than 30 seconds into your error log, and redo just those pieces tomorrow morning.
tasks.hi: Har woh command jis par 30 seconds se zyada sochna pada, apne error log mein likho, aur kal subah sirf wahi pieces dobara karo.

verify.hi: SW1 par show etherchannel summary — Po1(SU), F0/23-24 (P)

verify.en: show ip route on R1 — connected VLAN subnets plus O 192.168.30.0/24
verify.hi: R1 par show ip route — connected VLAN subnets plus O 192.168.30.0/24

verify.hi: R1 par show ip ospf neighbor — R2 FULL

verify.hi: PC1 se PC3, PC2 aur PC4 ko ping — teeno succeed

verify.hi: Timer — poora build 60 minutes ke andar complete

note.en: This is the exam's lab-sim format in miniature: requirements in, working config out. Speed comes from finger memory — if you stalled anywhere, that command belongs in tomorrow's warm-up.
note.hi: Yeh exam ke lab-sim format ka chhota roop hai: requirements andar, working config bahar. Speed finger memory se aati hai — agar kahin bhi atke, toh woh command kal ke warm-up mein jayegi.

title.en: Super Lab 2: Services + Security from Memory
title.hi: Super Lab 2: Services + Security Yaad se

objective.en: Rebuild the services and security stack — DHCP, PAT, NTP, SSH, an extended ACL and port security — from a requirements list, notes closed, in 60 minutes.
objective.hi: Services aur security stack — DHCP, PAT, NTP, SSH, ek extended ACL aur port security — ek requirements list se, notes band karke, 60 minutes mein dobara banao.

tasks.en: Set a 60-minute timer, notes closed. Build the topology: inside LAN 192.168.1.0/24 (R1 g0/0 = .1), R1-ISP link 198.51.100.0/30 (R1 = .1, ISP = .2), ISP LAN 203.0.113.0/24 (ISP g0/1 = .1, Server1 = .100). Default route on R1 only; the ISP knows nothing about 192.168.1.0/24.
tasks.hi: 60-minute timer set karo, notes band. Topology banao: inside LAN 192.168.1.0/24 (R1 g0/0 = .1), R1-ISP link 198.51.100.0/30 (R1 = .1, ISP = .2), ISP LAN 203.0.113.0/24 (ISP g0/1 = .1, Server1 = .100). Default route sirf R1 par; ISP ko 192.168.1.0/24 ke baare mein kuch nahi pata.

tasks.en: Requirement 1 — DHCP: IOS pool on R1 for the inside LAN (gateway .1, DNS 203.0.113.100, exclude .1-.49). PC1 and PC2 must lease addresses.
tasks.hi: Requirement 1 — DHCP: inside LAN ke liye R1 par IOS pool (gateway .1, DNS 203.0.113.100, .1-.49 exclude). PC1 aur PC2 ko addresses lease hone chahiye.

tasks.en: Requirement 2 — PAT: interface overload on R1 g0/1 for the whole inside LAN (standard ACL 1 as the match).
tasks.hi: Requirement 2 — PAT: poore inside LAN ke liye R1 g0/1 par interface overload (match ke liye standard ACL 1).

tasks.en: Requirement 3 — NTP: R1 synchronized to 203.0.113.100.
tasks.hi: Requirement 3 — NTP: R1 203.0.113.100 se synchronized.

tasks.en: Requirement 4 — SSH: R1 reachable ONLY by SSHv2 (domain ccna.lab, RSA 1024, user admin privilege 15 secret of your choosing, vty login local, transport input ssh, enable secret set).
tasks.hi: Requirement 4 — SSH: R1 SIRF SSHv2 se reachable ho (domain ccna.lab, RSA 1024, user admin privilege 15 apni pasand ke secret ke saath, vty login local, transport input ssh, enable secret set).

tasks.en: Requirement 5 — extended ACL: hosts in 192.168.1.0/24 may NOT open HTTP to Server1 but everything else (ping, NTP, DNS) must work — named ACL, applied inbound on R1 g0/0.
tasks.hi: Requirement 5 — extended ACL: 192.168.1.0/24 ke hosts Server1 par HTTP NAHI khol sakte lekin baaki sab (ping, NTP, DNS) chalna chahiye — named ACL, R1 g0/0 par inbound applied.

tasks.en: Requirement 6 — port security: SW1 F0/1-2 access ports, maximum 1 sticky MAC each, violation shutdown.
tasks.hi: Requirement 6 — port security: SW1 F0/1-2 access ports, har ek par maximum 1 sticky MAC, violation shutdown.

tasks.en: Requirement 7 — proof and backup: from PC1 confirm ping 203.0.113.100 works while the browser to it fails; SSH to R1 from PC1; then copy running-config tftp: to Server1.
tasks.hi: Requirement 7 — proof aur backup: PC1 se confirm karo ki ping 203.0.113.100 chalta hai jabki uska browser fail hota hai; PC1 se R1 par SSH karo; phir copy running-config tftp: Server1 par.

tasks.en: Grade with: show ip dhcp binding, show ip nat translations, show ntp status, show ip ssh, show access-lists (hit counts on the deny), show port-security. Score 7 requirements, log the gaps, and compare your time against lab-34's run.
tasks.hi: In se grade karo: show ip dhcp binding, show ip nat translations, show ntp status, show ip ssh, show access-lists (deny par hit counts), show port-security. 7 requirements score karo, gaps log karo, aur apna time lab-34 ke run se compare karo.

tasks.en: Save as final-superlab.pkt — reviewing this file the night before the exam is worth more than any video.
tasks.hi: final-superlab.pkt naam se save karo — exam se pehle wali raat yeh file review karna kisi bhi video se zyada kaam ka hai.

verify.hi: show ip dhcp binding — PC1 aur PC2 ki leases

verify.hi: show ip nat translations — ping test ke dauraan PAT entries

verify.hi: show ntp status — synchronized; show ip ssh — version 2 enabled

verify.hi: show port-security — dono ports secure-up, har ek par 1 sticky MAC

note.en: If you clear both super labs from memory inside the timebox, the configuration portion of the real exam holds nothing new — the rest is reading questions carefully.
note.hi: Agar tum dono super labs timebox ke andar yaad se clear kar lete ho, toh real exam ke configuration portion mein kuch naya nahi hai — baaki kaam bas questions dhyan se padhna hai.

objective.en: Walk into (or log into) the CCNA 200-301 exam with logistics, materials and strategy already decided, so every brain cycle goes to the questions.
objective.hi: CCNA 200-301 exam mein (ya online log in karke) aise jao ki logistics, materials aur strategy pehle se decide ho, taaki dimaag ki saari energy questions par lage.

topology: None — this is a preparation checklist, not a build

tasks.en: ID documents: lay out one valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID tonight (name must match your Pearson VUE registration EXACTLY — check the confirmation email now). Keep a second ID (bank card with name) as backup.
tasks.hi: ID documents: aaj raat hi ek valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID nikal kar rakh lo (naam tumhari Pearson VUE registration se BILKUL match hona chahiye — confirmation email abhi check karo). Backup ke liye ek second ID (naam wala bank card) rakho.

tasks.en: Logistics — test center: know the address, parking and travel time; plan to arrive 30 minutes early. Bring nothing extra — phones, watches, notes and even your own pen go into a locker.
tasks.hi: Logistics — test center: address, parking aur travel time pata hona chahiye; 30 minutes pehle pahunchne ka plan karo. Kuch extra mat lao — phones, watches, notes aur apna pen bhi locker mein jata hai.

tasks.en: Logistics — online (OnVUE): run the official system test on the SAME computer and network you will use, the day before. Clear your desk completely, ensure a quiet closed room, charge the laptop, close every background app, and be ready for the photo/room-scan check-in 30 minutes before start.
tasks.hi: Logistics — online (OnVUE): ek din pehle usi SAME computer aur network par official system test chalao jo tum use karoge. Desk poori tarah khaali karo, ek shaant band kamra pakka karo, laptop charge karo, har background app band karo, aur start se 30 minutes pehle photo/room-scan check-in ke liye taiyaar raho.

tasks.en: Whiteboard strategy: the moment the exam clock starts, spend 60-90 seconds dumping your subnetting aids onto the provided erasable board (or online whiteboard): block sizes 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1, mask octets 128 192 224 240 248 252 254 255, and the AD table (0, 1, 20, 90, 110, 120). Cheap insurance against pressure blanks.
tasks.hi: Whiteboard strategy: jaise hi exam clock start ho, 60-90 seconds lagakar apne subnetting aids diye gaye erasable board (ya online whiteboard) par utaar do: block sizes 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1, mask octets 128 192 224 240 248 252 254 255, aur AD table (0, 1, 20, 90, 110, 120). Pressure mein dimaag blank hone ke against yeh sasta insurance hai.

tasks.en: Time budget: about 120 minutes for about 100 questions is roughly 70 seconds each. Checkpoint yourself: question 25 by 30 minutes, question 50 by 60, question 75 by 90. Lab-sims deserve extra time — bank seconds on easy MCQs.
tasks.hi: Time budget: lagbhag 100 questions ke liye lagbhag 120 minutes, yaani har ek ke liye roughly 70 seconds. Khud ko checkpoint karo: 30 minutes tak question 25, 60 tak question 50, 90 tak question 75. Lab-sims ko extra time chahiye — easy MCQs par seconds bachao.

tasks.en: No back-navigation: the CCNA does NOT let you return to a previous question. Once you click Next, that answer is final — so never leave a question blank, and never carry the last question into the next one.
tasks.hi: Back-navigation nahi: CCNA tumhe pichhle question par wapas jaane NAHI deta. Ek baar Next click kiya toh woh answer final hai — isliye kabhi koi question blank mat chhodo, aur pichhle question ka tension agle mein mat le jao.

tasks.en: Decide-and-move mindset: if a question stumps you, eliminate the obviously wrong options, pick the best remaining answer, take one breath, and move on cleanly. One hard question is 1 percent; tilting for ten minutes costs eight questions.
tasks.hi: Decide-and-move mindset: agar koi question atka de, toh saaf galat options hatao, bache hue mein se best answer chuno, ek saans lo, aur saaf-saaf aage badho. Ek mushkil question 1 percent hai; das minute uspe tilt hone se aath questions ka nuksaan hota hai.

tasks.en: The night before: stop studying by early evening — review only your error log and the whiteboard dump, nothing new. Pack ID plus confirmation, set two alarms, and sleep a full night; sleep consolidates memory better than cramming.
tasks.hi: Pichhli raat: shaam jaldi padhai band kar do — sirf apna error log aur whiteboard dump review karo, kuch naya nahi. ID plus confirmation pack karo, do alarms lagao, aur poori raat soyo; neend memory ko cramming se behtar consolidate karti hai.

tasks.en: Exam morning: eat a normal meal, hydrate lightly (bathroom breaks cost exam time), arrive or log in early, and remind yourself: three mock exams above target means the pass is yours to keep, not to win.
tasks.hi: Exam ki subah: normal khana khao, thoda hi paani piyo (bathroom breaks exam ka time khate hain), jaldi pahuncho ya log in karo, aur khud ko yaad dilao: target se upar teen mock exams ka matlab hai pass tumhara hai, bas use sambhal kar rakhna hai, jeetna nahi.

tasks.en: After the exam: score report arrives quickly — whatever happens, write down every topic you remember struggling with while it is fresh.
tasks.hi: Exam ke baad: score report jaldi aa jati hai — jo bhi ho, jin topics par atke the woh sab abhi taaza yaad rehte hi likh lo.

verify.en: Night-before check — ID, confirmation email, route or system-test all confirmed
verify.hi: Pichhli raat ka check — ID, confirmation email, route ya system-test sab confirmed

verify.en: Whiteboard drill — you can write the full subnetting dump from memory in under 90 seconds
verify.hi: Whiteboard drill — tum poora subnetting dump yaad se 90 seconds se kam mein likh sakte ho

verify.en: Time plan — checkpoint numbers (25/30, 50/60, 75/90) memorized
verify.hi: Time plan — checkpoint numbers (25/30, 50/60, 75/90) yaad hain

verify.en: Mindset check — you can state the no-back-navigation rule and your flag-and-move response to a stumper
verify.hi: Mindset check — tum no-back-navigation rule aur atkane wale question par apna flag-and-move response bata sakte ho

note.en: You prepared for 8 weeks; exam day is just execution. Trust the checkpoints, trust the whiteboard, and let the easy questions pay for the hard ones.
note.hi: Tumne 8 hafte taiyaari ki hai; exam day bas execution hai. Checkpoints par bharosa rakho, whiteboard par bharosa rakho, aur easy questions ko hard questions ki kimat chukane do.
